front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates as a Pennsylvania licensed long-term care residence. It is written for the program types licensed by the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS), Office of Long-Term Living (OLTL), Bureau of Human Services Licensing (BHSL):

- **Assisted Living Residence (ALR)**, governed by 55 Pa. Code Chapter 2800
- **Personal Care Home (PCH)**, governed by 55 Pa. Code Chapter 2600

The manual has four aims:

1. **Protect residents.** It puts into daily practice the rules on resident rights, abuse and incident reporting, medication safety, fire and emergency preparedness, staffing, nutrition and discharge.
2. **Support licensure.** It gives BHSL the written policies and plans it reviews before an initial license is issued, or before a sale or change of legal entity is approved. It also supports the annual unannounced inspection and any reinspection.
3. **Give staff one reference.** It tells administrators, designees, direct care staff and substitutes what to do, who is responsible and what to document.
4. **Support quality management.** It provides the baseline that the residence's quality management plan reviews and improves over time.

**Payment context.** Residence charges at [AGENCY NAME] are mostly private pay. Medicaid long-term services and supports are delivered through Community HealthChoices and generally do not cover PCH or ALR residence charges. Policies on contracts, fees, refunds and SSI recipients therefore need particular care. Where a resident is SSI-eligible, the SSI rules apply.

**Scope note.** Chapter 2800 states that it does not apply to personal care homes, domiciliary care homes, independent living communities or commercial boarding homes (55 Pa. Code §2800.2). A residence licensed as an ALR follows Chapter 2800. A residence licensed as a PCH follows Chapter 2600. Only the licensed term "assisted living" may be used for a licensed ALR (55 Pa. Code §2800.11).

# How to Use This Manual

## Who should use it
The manual is for the administrator, the administrator's written designee, direct care staff, ancillary staff, substitutes and volunteers. The governing body uses it to oversee compliance. Resident-facing sections (rights, complaints, contracts, discharge) are written so staff can explain them accurately to residents and designated persons.

## How it is organized
Policies are grouped by subject, for example rights and complaints, admission and contracts, staffing and training, medications, fire safety and emergency preparedness, and records. Each policy states its purpose, the regulatory cite it implements, who is responsible, the steps to follow and what to document.

## Appendix A: the cross-reference to the official checklist
The state reviews this manual against its official prelicensure checklists, which are named in the Regulatory Framework section. **Appendix A maps every official checklist item to the policy in this manual that satisfies it.** Use it in three ways:

- Before submission, confirm that each checklist item has a matching policy and that nothing is missing.
- During a BHSL review, locate the policy for any item by the checklist's own numbering. BHSL may ask for materials in a different order than the checklist lists them.
- When a regulation or checklist changes, find every affected policy.

## Customizing the manual (required)
This manual is a template. Before use:

1. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed field with the residence's own information. This includes the legal entity, license type (ALR and/or PCH), licensed capacity, administrator and designee names, and local emergency, fire and agency contacts.
2. Delete or complete sections that apply only if the residence offers the service. Examples are special care unit (ALR) or secured dementia care unit (PCH) policies, smoking, firearms and weapons, pets, swimming pool and resident fund management.
3. Confirm that each policy matches how the residence actually operates. A written policy the residence does not follow is a compliance risk.
4. For a PCH, verify each policy against the current text of 55 Pa. Code Chapter 2600. Most rule summaries used to build this manual come from Chapter 2800.

## Adoption by the governing body (required)
The governing body of [AGENCY NAME] must formally adopt the customized manual by resolution or recorded vote. Record the adoption date and signatories on the adoption page. Re-adopt after any significant revision.

## Keeping it current (required)
- Review the manual at least annually and whenever a regulation, checklist, DHS form, license condition, waiver, service or physical plant changes.
- Check the current Pa. Code text and current DHS forms, fees and checklist versions before relying on any figure or form in this manual.
- Record revisions on a revision log (date, section, reason, approver). Feed review results into the quality management plan.
- Keep a copy on site where staff can reach it. Keep the posted items required by regulation, such as the license, inspection summary and a copy of the regulations, in a conspicuous public place.

## Staff training (required)
All staff must be trained on this manual:

- Give each new staff member, substitute and volunteer the policies relevant to their duties during orientation, and document it.
- Re-train when a policy is revised.
- Keep signed acknowledgments and training records, and tie them to the annual staff training plan.
- Make sure staff know where the manual is kept and whom to ask when a situation is not covered.

## A note on legal effect
This manual implements the regulations. It does not replace them. If anything here conflicts with a statute, regulation or DHS direction, the legal requirement controls. Report the conflict to the administrator so the manual can be corrected. Obtain legal or licensing advice for specific situations.

DHS licenses personal care homes and assisted living residences under the state plan authorized by **62 P.S. §211**. | **PA DHS Bureau of Human Services Licensing (BHSL)** | Pre-licensure inspection, annual unannounced inspection, complaint and incident investigation, reinspection within 3 months of initial licensure. | 717-783-3670 · ra-pwarlheadquarters@pa.gov · https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/departments-offices/oltl-info/oltl-bureau-human-services-licensing |
| **BHSL Operator Support Hotline** | Answers licensing-process questions from PCH and ALR operators and applicants. Hours: 9 a.m.–4 p.m. each Commonwealth business day. | (866) 503-3926 · https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/resources/licensing/pch-alr-licensing/pch-alr-contact |
| **BHSL complaint / illegal-operation line** | Report illegal operations and complaints. The ALR complaint hotline number must be posted in large print in the residence (§2800.44(g)). | 1-877-401-8835 · https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/resources/licensing/pch-alr-licensing/pch-alr-contact |
| **Human Services Provider Directory (DHS)** | Public search of licensed PCHs and ALRs by zip code, county and region. Refreshed daily. | https://www.humanservices.dhs.pa.gov/human_service_provider_directory/ |

The rules also give access or complaint roles to the area agency on aging, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, the protective services unit, the Pennsylvania protection and advocacy system (Disability Rights Network), local police, and the local fire department and emergency management agency. The materials used to prepare this manual did not supply contact details for these entities. **[AGENCY NAME] must insert current local numbers in the designated contact fields and on the postings required by §2800.44 and §2800.107.**

## Official policy checklists used to review this manual
DHS BHSL reviews a residence's written policies against its official pre-inspection checklists. The packet is submitted to the BHSL headquarters office before the initial inspection of a new facility, or of a sale or change of legal entity, is scheduled. The checklists are:

1. **Pre-Inspection Checklist for New Assisted Living Residences (ALR) and ALR Sale or Change of Legal Entity** (web title: *Assisted Living Residences (ALR) Prelicensure Checklist*). Issued by PA DHS BHSL, revised 1/14/25, 4 pages, no form number printed (file: alr-prelicensure-checklist-1-14-2025.pdf). This is the primary document for Chapter 2800. https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dhs/documents/providers/clearances-and-licensing/documents/app-hsl/alr-prelicensure-checklist-1-14-2025.pdf
2. **Pre-Inspection Checklist for New Personal Care Homes (PCH) and PCH Sale or Change of Legal Entity** (web title: *Personal Care Home (PCH) Prelicensure Checklist*). Issued by PA DHS BHSL, revised 1/14/25, 4 pages, no form number printed (file: pch-prelicensure-checklist-1-15-2025.pdf). This is the primary document for Chapter 2600. It has the same structure as the ALR checklist, with Chapter 2600 citations and secured dementia care unit (SDCU) wording in place of special care unit (SCU). https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dhs/documents/providers/clearances-and-licensing/documents/app-hsl/pch-prelicensure-checklist-1-15-2025.pdf

A residence licensed as an ALR submits the ALR checklist. A PCH submits the PCH checklist. The two are separate.

*Superseded document:* an older, undated list titled "Policies and Procedures, 55 Pa. Code Chapter 2800 – Assisted Living Residences" (the Chapter 2800 Policy Review List) appears to be replaced by the 1/14/25 ALR checklist. It is noted here only so it is not mistaken for the current document. Confirm the current version with BHSL before submitting.

**How this manual maps to the checklists.** The checklists are numbered 1–18, with lettered sub-items. The policy and plan items (for example item 8(a), Reportable Incidents and Conditions Policy, §2800.16(b)) are the content this manual supplies. Application and evidence items are not policies, so the manual does not contain them. These are administrator credentials, the criminal history clearances themselves, floor plans, the elevator certificate, SCU/SDCU site evidence, the written SCU/SDCU request, and checklist items 11–18. Checklist item 10 lists forms, such as the contract, rights poster, fire drill record, assessment and support plan forms and the medication administration record. This manual treats those as operating documents. **Appendix A maps every official checklist item to the policy in this manual that satisfies it, and identifies the items that are handled outside the manual.** BHSL may request additional materials, or the same materials in a different order, so keep Appendix A current.

## Customization, adoption, currency and training
This manual is not ready for use or submission until it has been:

- **Customized.** All **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholders and bracketed fields are completed for the specific residence, license type and services.
- **Adopted** by the governing body, with the adoption recorded.
- **Kept current** through at least annual review, and updated whenever a rule, checklist, form, fee or the residence's operations change.
- **Taught to staff.** All staff, substitutes and volunteers are trained on the policies that apply to them, with documentation kept on file.

citations.title: Scope
citations.requirement: Ch. 2800 sets minimum licensure requirements for assisted living residences and does not apply to personal care homes, domiciliary care homes, independent living communities or commercial boarding homes. (Text is from a DHS-hosted Pa. Code print; confirm no later amendments.)

citations.title: Inspections and licenses
citations.requirement: DHS makes at least one unannounced onsite inspection a year. The residence must post the current license, the current inspection summary and a copy of Ch. 2800 in a conspicuous public place.

citations.title: Access
citations.requirement: Give immediate access to the residence, residents and records on request to DHS agents, the area agency on aging, the LTC Ombudsman, the P&A system and, if the resident asks, the designated person. Community and legal-services groups get access during visiting hours.

citations.title: Procedural requirements for licensure; special care designation; dual licensure
citations.requirement: DHS inspects before initial licensure and reinspects within 3 months. Fees are $300 plus $75 per bed (per-bed fee CPI-adjustable). Special care designation costs $150. Only licensees may use the term 'assisted living'.

citations.title: Maximum capacity
citations.requirement: Licensed capacity may not be exceeded. A request to increase capacity must be approved by DHS and other authorities before additional residents are admitted.

citations.title: Fire safety approval
citations.requirement: Written fire safety approval is required before licensure. If it is withdrawn or restricted, notify DHS orally at once and in writing within 48 hours. After renovation, submit new approval within 15 days. Renew at least every 3 years.

citations.title: Abuse reporting covered by law
citations.requirement: Immediately report suspected abuse under the Older Adult Protective Services Act and 6 Pa. Code §§15.21–15.27. For staff allegations, supervise or suspend the person at once, notify DHS immediately, and notify the resident and designated person.

citations.title: Reportable incidents and conditions – list and policies
citations.requirement: Defines 20 reportable incidents or conditions, including death, hospital-level injury, rights violations, unexplained absence, fund misuse, outbreaks, fire, med errors and utility termination. Written prevention, reporting and investigation policies are required.

citations.title: Reportable incidents – timelines and reports
citations.requirement: Report to the DHS ALR office or hotline within 24 hours, and tell family and the designated person immediately. Submit a final report on the DHS form after the investigation. Inform affected residents if validated. Keep a copy.

citations.title: Confidentiality of records
citations.requirement: Resident records are confidential. Without written consent, only the resident, designated person, staff providing services, DHS agents and the ombudsman may see them, except in emergencies or on court order.

citations.title: Applicable laws
citations.requirement: The residence must comply with applicable Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations. Violations of health and safety laws are themselves reportable under §2800.16(a)(19).

citations.title: Waivers
citations.requirement: Waivers use the DHS form and require no jeopardy to residents. They get a 30-day public comment period, and residents must be given the request 30 days before it is submitted. Rights, contract, reporting, fire safety, assessment and training rules cannot be waived.

citations.title: Financial management
citations.requirement: If handling resident funds: keep transaction records, disburse within 24 hours, get written receipts, never commingle, and offer an interest-bearing account if over $200 is held more than 2 months. Staff may not hold POA or guardianship. Give itemized quarterly accounts.

citations.title: Application and admission – documents and certification
citations.requirement: Medical evaluation within 60 days before admission and initial assessment within 30 days before. Final support plan within 30 days after admission and contract by 24 hours after. Certify before admission that needs can be met. If not, give a written denial and refer.

citations.title: Written disclosures before admission
citations.requirement: On application, give the non-waivable rights list, the contract, rules and the DHS-approved handbook. Also give service and core-package costs, DHS contact info, inspection-report access, ADA-compliant unit count and any waivers in effect.

citations.title: Resident-residence contract
citations.requirement: The contract runs month-to-month, with 14 days' resident notice and 30 days' residence notice. It must include a fee schedule, refund terms and bed-hold charges. Residents have a 72-hour rescission right, and no life-care asset assignment is allowed.

citations.title: Quality management
citations.requirement: Establish and implement a quality management plan. It must periodically review incident reporting, complaints, staff training, violations and plans of correction, and councils, and it must carry out improvement measures.

citations.title: SSI recipients
citations.requirement: If an SSI-eligible resident is admitted, charges may not exceed monthly income minus the personal needs allowance. Provide hygiene items, laundry and ADL/IADL help at no extra charge. Third-party payments may not be used for food, clothing or shelter.

citations.title: Refunds
citations.requirement: Refund prepaid charges within 30 days of discharge, the personal needs allowance within 2 business days, and managed funds within 2 business days of the unit being cleared. Give an itemized account within 30 days. Death refunds follow the Elder Care Payment Restitution Act for age 60+.

citations.title: Hospice care and services
citations.requirement: Hospice care and services licensed by the Department of Health may be provided in an assisted living residence.

citations.title: Informed consent process
citations.requirement: Either party may start the process when a competent resident's choices create risk. Give oral and written notice with the ombudsman's contact. Put any agreement in writing, update it on condition change, and allow rescission within 30 days. It may not be a condition of admission.

citations.title: Notification of rights and complaint procedures
citations.requirement: At admission, inform residents and designated persons of rights and the right to complain without retaliation. Use a language or mode they understand and post the DHS rights poster. Give a copy and keep a signed acknowledgment.

citations.title: Specific rights
citations.requirement: Rights include non-discrimination, freedom from abuse and restraints, 30 days' written notice of new rules, private phone and mail, ombudsman access, visitors at any time, privacy, records access, physician choice, and relocation assistance.

citations.title: Prohibition against deprivation of rights
citations.requirement: A resident may not be deprived of rights. Rights may not be used as a reward or sanction, and any waiver of a right is void.

citations.title: Complaint procedures
citations.requirement: Before admission, inform residents of the right to complain to DHS, the ombudsman or protective services unit, the Disability Rights Network or police. Keep a complaint log, give a status report within 2 business days and a written decision within 7 days. Post hotline and agency numbers in large print.

citations.title: Criminal history checks; staff hiring, retention and utilization
citations.requirement: Criminal history checks, hiring policies and staff retention must comply with the Older Adult Protective Services Act, 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15, and the Department of Aging's OAPSA hiring policy.

citations.title: Qualifications and responsibilities of administrators
citations.requirement: Administrator must be age 21+ and qualify by RN license plus 1 year of experience in the past 10 years, or by one of the other listed paths. Responsible for operations and compliance. Must know Ch. 2800 and be free of impairing conditions.

citations.title: Qualifications for direct care staff persons
citations.requirement: Direct care staff must be 18+, hold a diploma, GED or active PA nurse aide registry status, and be free of impairing conditions. Volunteers giving ADL help meet the same standards. Food service or housekeeping staff may be 16–17.

citations.title: Administrator staffing
citations.requirement: Administrator present an average of 36+ hours a week each calendar month, at least 30 during business hours. Name a written designee (3,000 operational hours plus competency test) and a written staff person for absences. The administrator or designee must be on call.

citations.title: Direct care staffing; awake staff
citations.requirement: A direct care staff person age 21+ must be in the residence whenever residents are present. Provide at least 1 hour per day of services per mobile resident and 2 hours per day per resident with mobility needs, with 75% in waking hours. Direct care staff must be awake at all times.

citations.title: Additional staffing based on needs of residents
citations.requirement: Staffing must meet assessed needs and the stated levels are only a minimum. Extra hours are required for transportation, laundry, food service, housekeeping and maintenance. A licensed nurse must be available or on call at all times, and a dietician on staff or contract.

citations.title: Substitute personnel; list of staff persons
citations.requirement: Arrange substitutes who meet direct care qualifications and training when scheduled staff are absent. Keep a current list of names, addresses and phone numbers for all staff, substitutes and volunteers.

citations.title: First aid, CPR and obstructed airway training
citations.requirement: For every 35 residents, at least one staff person trained in first aid and certified in obstructed airway and CPR must be present at all times. Training must come from a certified trainer. Staff must provide CPR unless the resident has a DNR.

citations.title: Administrator training and orientation
citations.requirement: Before employment: DHS orientation, a 100-hour DHS-approved course and a passing competency test. Then at least 24 hours of annual training from DHS-approved sources, with written verification to the ALR Licensing Office. Keep training records.

citations.title: Staff orientation and direct care staff person training
citations.requirement: Fire and emergency orientation on the first work day. Rights, abuse reporting, incident reporting and safe management within 40 working hours. No unsupervised care until 18 hours of training and the competency test. 16 hours annually, plus annual fire, rights, OAPSA and falls topics.

citations.title: Staff training plan
citations.requirement: Develop an annual training plan listing each direct care staff person's name, position, duties, required courses and scheduled dates, times and locations. Keep documentation of compliance.

citations.title: Additional dementia-specific training
citations.requirement: Administrative, direct care, ancillary and substitute staff and volunteers need 4 hours of dementia-specific training within 30 days of hire and 2 hours annually, in addition to other required training.

citations.title: Sanitation
citations.requirement: Maintain sanitary conditions with no insect or rodent infestation. Remove trash at least weekly and keep it in covered receptacles. Homes serving 9+ residents on private sewer need written sewage-system approval.

citations.title: Resident living units
citations.requirement: Single units need 225 sq ft in new construction after 1/18/2011 and 160 sq ft in existing facilities. Maximum is 2 residents per unit, and sharing is voluntary and in writing. Each unit needs a lockable door with a master key, a phone jack, thermostats and an emergency notification system.

citations.title: Food service; dining room; laundry
citations.requirement: Safe food storage: refrigerated at or below 40°F, frozen at or below 0°F, with thermometers. Common dining space at 15 sq ft per person. Linens changed at least weekly and clothing returned within 24 hours. Laundry is free for SSI residents.

citations.title: Emergency preparedness
citations.requirement: Administrator must have the municipal emergency plan. Written procedures cover designated contacts, medical information, agency numbers, relocation transport, staff duties and utility outages. Keep a 3-day food and water supply. Review and submit the procedures annually to the local EMA.

citations.title: Firearms and weapons; pets
citations.requirement: Have a written weapons policy (locked cabinet, separate ammunition, key held by the administrator or designee). Rules must say whether pets are allowed. Cats and dogs need current rabies certificates, and pet charges go in the contract.

citations.title: Egress, exits, evacuation and fire official notice
citations.requirement: Egress routes stay unlocked and unobstructed. Two independent exits per floor. Post emergency procedures, and post floor diagrams if 9+ residents. A fire-safe area is required for mobility-need residents above or below grade. Notify the local fire department in writing.

citations.title: Smoke detectors, fire alarms and fire extinguishers
citations.requirement: Smoke detector in each living unit, tested monthly with a written record. Repair within 48 hours. Interconnected alarm if 9+ residents, and a monitored connection if 5+ have mobility needs. 2-A extinguishers per floor and every 3,000 sq ft, plus 2A-10BC in the kitchen. Annual inspection.

citations.title: Fire drills
citations.requirement: Unannounced drill monthly, one during sleeping hours every 6 months, and an annual fire safety expert inspection and drill. Vary days, times and exits. Written record per drill. Residents must evacuate within the time set in writing by a fire safety expert.

citations.title: Resident medical evaluation and health care
citations.requirement: Medical evaluation on the DHS form by a physician, PA or CRNP covering diagnosis, allergies, medications, mobility and a TB test within 2 years (or within 15 days of admission). Repeat at least annually and when the medical condition changes.

citations.title: Assistance with medical care; emergency medical plan
citations.requirement: Help residents secure medical care. Document refusals and efforts to obtain consent. Keep a written emergency medical plan (hospital, transport, staffing). Emergency data, including advance directives and DNR, must go with the resident.

citations.title: Use of tobacco
citations.requirement: Residence rules must say whether it is smoking or nonsmoking. If smoking is permitted, adopt written fire-safety policies: designated area, fireproof receptacles, extinguishers, no tobacco use during transportation, and no smoking outside the designated area.

citations.title: Nutrition; meals; withholding or forcing food
citations.requirement: Three meals daily meeting USDA allowances, with an alternative item, plus snacks. Maximum gaps are 15 hours overnight and 6 hours between meals. One-week menus posted. Meet prescribed diets. Notify the physician and designated person if a resident refuses food or drink for 24 hours.

citations.title: Transportation
citations.requirement: Provide or arrange transport weekly. Drivers must be 18+ and licensed. Vehicles need a first aid kit and records (registration, insurance, inspection), and one wheelchair-accessible vehicle if supplied. Pick up within 15 minutes of the scheduled time.

citations.title: Self-administration; medication administration
citations.requirement: Assist with self-administration per assessment, and a physician, PA or CRNP must assess residents who self-administer. Staff may administer only if licensed or if they completed DHS-approved training (oral, topical, eye/nose/ear, insulin, epinephrine).

citations.title: Medication storage, disposal, labeling and accountability
citations.requirement: Keep medications and syringes locked in labeled original containers, and do not remove them more than 2 hours before administration. Destroy discontinued or expired medications safely, and send a departing resident's medications along. Keep receipt documentation and a missing-medication process.

citations.title: Prescriptions, medication records, errors and adverse reactions
citations.requirement: Written prescriber orders and a medication record per administration. Report refusals to the prescriber within 24 hours. Report errors immediately to the resident, designated person and prescriber. Document errors and follow-up. Consult a physician at once for adverse reactions.

citations.title: Medication administration training; resident education
citations.requirement: Medication course with performance test passed within the past 2 years. Insulin also requires DHS-approved diabetes education within the past 12 months. Keep training records. Educate and document each resident's right to question or refuse a medication.

citations.title: Safe management techniques; prohibitions; bedside rails
citations.requirement: Use positive interventions. Seclusion, aversive conditioning, pressure points, and chemical, mechanical and manual restraints are prohibited. Bedside rails only if the resident can operate them, with half-length rails only and documented assessment and consent.

citations.title: Service provision; activities; description of services
citations.requirement: Provide the §2800.220(b) service list (meals, laundry, activities, ADL/IADL help, medication help, housekeeping, transport, 24-hour supervision, cognitive support) and Independent and Enhanced core packages. Keep a written description of services with admission and discharge criteria and written procedures.

citations.title: Assessments and support plans
citations.requirement: Initial assessment and preliminary support plan by an RN, LPN under RN, administrator or designee. Reassess annually and on significant change. Final support plan within 30 days of admission, reviewed quarterly, signed, and given to the resident. Notify DHS of mobility needs.

citations.title: Transfer and discharge
citations.requirement: Give 30 days' written notice stating reason, date, destination and ombudsman contact. Closure needs 60 days' notice to DHS. Discharge is allowed only on the listed grounds, with aging-in-place accommodation attempted first. Keep a discharge tracking chart.

citations.title: Excludable conditions; exceptions
citations.requirement: Do not admit or retain residents with ventilator dependency, unhealed Stage III/IV ulcers, continuous IV fluids, communicable-state infectious disease, NG tubes, restraints or 24-hour skilled nursing, unless DHS grants an exception. Keep exception records.

citations.title: Special care units (dementia)
citations.requirement: Apply 60 days before opening a unit. Cognitive screening within 72 hours before admission and quarterly reassessment. 8 hours' initial and 8 hours' annual staff training. Weekly activities, lock approvals, wandering measures, and the 2-hour-per-day staffing rule for every resident.

citations.title: Resident records
citations.requirement: Separate on-site record per resident with the 28 required content items. Retain for 3 years after death or discharge or until audit or litigation ends. Destroy confidentially with a destruction log. Adopt a written record security policy, with records kept locked.

citations.title: Enforcement: violation classes, penalties, revocation, ban on admissions
citations.requirement: Class I violations are $20 per resident per day and must be corrected within 24 hours. Class II is $5–$15 per resident per day. Operating unlicensed is $500 plus $20 per resident per day. Residents must be notified of violations. DHS may ban admissions.

citations.title: Procedural requirements for licensure of personal care homes (PCH)
citations.requirement: PCHs are inspected before licensure and reinspected within 3 months. Application fee by beds: $15 (0–20), $20 (21–50), $30 (51–100), $50 (101+). Ch. 20 applies to PCHs.

citations.title: State plan for regulating and licensing PCHs and ALRs
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for DHS licensing of personal care homes and assisted living residences, including at least one annual unannounced onsite inspection of each.

policies.title: Administrator Qualifications, Orientation, Annual Training, Presence and Designee
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800); administrator, designee, owner/operator and Human Resources
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] is always directed by an administrator who meets the qualifications, orientation, training and on-site presence requirements of 55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800, and that a qualified designee is always available.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will employ an administrator who is at least 21 years old and who qualifies under 55 Pa. Code §2800.53. The qualifying paths are an RN license plus 1 year of experience within the past 10 years, or one of the other paths listed in §2800.53. The administrator must know Chapter 2800 and be free of any physical, mental or substance-related condition that would impair the ability to perform the duties. The administrator is responsible for operations and for regulatory compliance. Before starting work, the administrator must complete the DHS orientation, a 100-hour DHS-approved administrator course and a passing competency test (§2800.64). After that, the administrator must complete at least 24 hours of annual training from DHS-approved sources. Written verification of that training is sent to the ALR Licensing Office. The administrator will be present in the residence an average of at least 36 hours per week in each calendar month, with at least 30 of those hours during business hours (§2800.56). [AGENCY NAME] will name in writing a designee who has at least 3,000 operational hours and has passed the competency test. [AGENCY NAME] will also name in writing a staff person to be in charge during absences. The administrator or designee will be on call at all times. This policy addresses administrator qualifications, orientation, training, staffing and designee requirements as they apply to the license application.

definitions.definition: The person designated by [AGENCY NAME] who is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the residence and its compliance with Chapter 2800.
A person named in writing who has at least 3,000 operational hours and has passed the competency test, and who may act for the administrator.
Monday through Friday, [BUSINESS HOURS], excluding holidays observed by the residence, as stated in the posted schedule.
Total administrator hours on site in a calendar month divided by the number of weeks in that month.
Hours actually worked in the operation of a personal care home or assisted living residence, as documented in the designee's personnel file.

procedures: Before offering the administrator position, the owner/operator reviews the candidate's age, license or degree, work history and references against §2800.53 and records which qualification path applies.

The owner/operator obtains and files copies of the RN license (if that is the path) or the other documents that prove the qualification path. The owner/operator verifies the license on the PA licensing website and prints the verification.

The owner/operator confirms that the candidate has completed the DHS orientation, the 100-hour DHS-approved course and a passing competency test. Certificates are filed before the first day of employment. The candidate does not act as administrator until this is complete.

The candidate completes a statement that he or she is free of any condition that would impair the ability to perform the duties. This is placed in the personnel file with the clearances required under CHK-01.
The administrator reads Chapter 2800 and [AGENCY NAME] policies and signs an acknowledgment within 7 days of hire. The signed acknowledgment is filed in the personnel file.
The owner/operator names the designee in writing. The designee's 3,000 operational hours are verified through prior employer letters or equivalent proof, and the competency test result is filed.

The owner/operator names in writing a staff person to be in charge when both the administrator and designee are absent. The designation states who covers which hours and is posted at the staff station.
The administrator records actual hours on site each day on the Administrator Hours Log (start, end, business hours versus other). The administrator signs the log weekly.

On the first business day after each month closes, the owner/operator totals the log and calculates the weekly average. The average must be at least 36 hours, with at least 30 during business hours. Any month below standard is documented with a corrective action plan.
A written on-call schedule shows who (administrator or designee) is on call each day, with a phone number. The schedule is posted and given to all shift supervisors.

At the start of each calendar year, the administrator and owner/operator develop an annual training plan to total at least 24 hours from DHS-approved sources. The plan is filed in the training record (see PLAN-01).

The administrator logs each training session as completed (title, source, date, hours, certificate). The owner/operator checks the log each quarter to confirm the administrator is on track to reach 24 hours.

By the date required by the ALR Licensing Office, the owner/operator sends written verification of the administrator's annual training to the ALR Licensing Office. A copy and proof of delivery are kept.

If the administrator leaves or is unable to serve, the owner/operator names the designee as acting administrator at once and notifies the licensing office as required. The owner/operator then recruits a replacement who meets this policy before assuming duties.
The owner/operator reviews this policy and the administrator's file every year and whenever the regulations change.

responsibilities.duty: Verify administrator and designee qualifications, name the designee and the person in charge in writing, review the hours log monthly and ensure training verification is sent.
Meet the on-site hours standard, remain on call or arrange the designee, complete 24 hours of annual training and keep the logs current.
Act for the administrator during absences, remain current on competency and be on call when scheduled.
Maintain personnel and training files and prepare the written verification for the ALR Licensing Office.

documentation: Administrator qualification file (license, degree or other proof, license verification printout)
DHS orientation certificate, 100-hour course certificate and competency test result
Impairing-condition statement and signed Chapter 2800 acknowledgment
Written designee appointment with proof of 3,000 operational hours and test result
Written designation of staff person in charge during absences
Administrator Hours Log and monthly average calculation
On-call schedule
Annual training plan, training log, certificates and copy of verification sent to the ALR Licensing Office

policies.category: 2. Criminal history background checks (2(b): policy and procedures for future staff, retention and utilization)
policies.title: Criminal History Clearances, Staff Retention and Utilization (OAPSA)
policies.applies_to: ALR (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800; PCH parallel under Ch. 2600); all employees, owners/operators who work in the residence, and Human Resources
policies.purpose: To make sure criminal history clearances are obtained for all staff hired, and that staff are hired, retained and used in accordance with the Older Adult Protective Services Act (OAPSA), 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15 and the Department of Aging's OAPSA hiring policy.
policies.policy: This policy meets checklist item 2(b), "policy and procedures for conducting criminal history clearances for all future staff to be hired, as well as retention and utilization of staff in accordance with OAPSA" (checklist cite § 2600.51, 52; ALR equivalent §§2800.51–2800.52). [AGENCY NAME] will obtain the criminal history clearances required by OAPSA and 6 Pa. Code Chapter 15 for every person it hires, and for the owner/operator who works in the residence. Hiring, retention and utilization decisions will follow the Department of Aging's OAPSA hiring policy. An owner/operator who is not a Pennsylvania resident and who will work in the residence must also provide an FBI background check. No applicant will be placed in a position with resident contact unless the clearances and hiring rules of OAPSA and the Department of Aging policy are met. The results are kept in each personnel file. A staff person who is the subject of an abuse allegation will be supervised or suspended at once as required by §2800.15, and DHS, the resident and the designated person will be notified (see SAF-01).

definitions.definition: The Older Adult Protective Services Act and its regulations at 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15, which require criminal history checks and set limits on employment of persons with certain convictions.
The criminal history record check(s) required by OAPSA and the Department of Aging hiring policy, including the FBI check when required.
The duties a staff person is allowed to perform based on clearance results, including whether the person may have unsupervised resident contact.
Continuing the employment of a staff person after hire, including after new information on criminal history or an abuse allegation.

procedures: The job application asks about criminal convictions and states that employment is conditional on clearance results under OAPSA. The applicant signs the disclosure.
Before a job offer is final, Human Resources reviews the Department of Aging's OAPSA hiring policy and confirms which clearances apply to the position and to the applicant's residency history.
Human Resources gives the applicant the clearance request forms and instructions on the day of the interview. The applicant or [AGENCY NAME] submits the requests as OAPSA directs.
Human Resources logs the date each clearance was requested and the date the result was received on the Clearance Tracking Log.
Where the applicant has not lived in Pennsylvania for the period required by OAPSA, Human Resources requests the FBI background check in addition to the state check.
If the owner/operator is not a Pennsylvania resident and will work in the residence, the owner/operator obtains an FBI background check before working, and a copy is filed.

Human Resources compares each result against the disqualifying offenses and time limits in OAPSA and the Department of Aging hiring policy. A result that is a prohibited offense ends the hiring process, and the decision is documented.

Where OAPSA allows provisional employment pending a result, the administrator documents that the conditions are met. The person works only under continuous direct supervision of a cleared staff person and has no unsupervised resident contact until the result is received.

When a result discloses a conviction, the administrator and Human Resources review the offense, date and relation to the job. They document the decision on the Clearance Review Form, applying the OAPSA hiring policy without exception.
Original results are filed in the personnel file. The file is stored in a locked cabinet and is not shared outside the legal and regulatory purposes described in POL-02.
Each employee must notify the administrator within 24 hours of any arrest, charge or conviction after hire. The administrator reviews the matter the next business day.

When a staff person has an arrest or conviction after hire, or an OAPSA hiring-policy issue arises, the administrator removes the person from unsupervised resident contact until the matter is reviewed. The review is documented, and the person is retained, reassigned or terminated as OAPSA permits.

If a resident, family member or staff person alleges abuse by a staff person, the administrator immediately removes that person from resident contact (supervision or suspension). The administrator reports to DHS immediately and notifies the resident and designated person as required by §2800.15 and SAF-01.

Before a staff person's first shift, the administrator completes the Pre-Placement Checklist confirming that clearances are on file, that the position and supervision level match the clearance result, and that required qualifications are met (see TRN-01).
The administrator audits all personnel files every six months for missing clearances or results and reports findings to the owner/operator. Gaps are corrected within 5 business days.
[AGENCY NAME] reviews this policy annually and whenever OAPSA, 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15 or the Department of Aging hiring policy changes.

responsibilities.duty: Request clearances, track results, compare results to OAPSA and maintain the personnel files and Clearance Tracking Log.
Make hire, retention and utilization decisions, supervise provisional employees, remove staff from resident contact when needed and perform audits.
Obtain own clearances (including FBI check if required) and review audit findings.
Disclose arrests, charges and convictions within 24 hours and cooperate with clearance requests.

documentation: Application with signed conviction disclosure
Clearance Tracking Log (request and result dates)
Criminal history clearance results and FBI check (when required) in each personnel file
Clearance Review Form for any result with a conviction
Provisional employment supervision record (if used)
Pre-Placement Checklist
Six-month personnel file audit report

policies.title: Planned Staffing Patterns, Shifts and Duties
policies.applies_to: ALR (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800; PCH parallel under Ch. 2600); administrator, shift supervisors and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To set the planned staffing pattern, shifts and duties for staff hired and to be hired, based on every service in the description of services, so that resident needs are met at all hours.
policies.policy: This policy meets checklist item 3, "the planned staffing patterns/shifts/duties of staff hired/to be hired based upon all services offered in the description of services" (checklist cite § 2600.56(a), § 2600.57(a)–(d), § 2600.233(a)–(b); ALR equivalents §§2800.56, 2800.57, 2800.60 and 2800.233). A direct care staff person who is at least 21 years old will be in the residence whenever one or more residents are present (§2800.57). [AGENCY NAME] will provide at least 1 hour per day of assisted living services for each mobile resident and at least 2 hours per day for each resident with mobility needs, with at least 75% of those hours provided during waking hours. Those levels are a minimum. Staffing will be set from each resident's assessment and support plan and will include the additional hours needed for food service, laundry, housekeeping, maintenance and transportation (§2800.60). If a special care unit (SCU) is operated, [AGENCY NAME] will provide at least 2 hours of staffing per day for every SCU resident (§§2800.233 and 2800.238). The administrator will be present an average of at least 36 hours per week each calendar month (§2800.56). A shift and duty chart for each service offered is attached to this policy as Attachment A and is part of the application.

definitions.definition: A resident who is able to move about the residence without the physical assistance of another person, as determined by the assessment.
A resident who needs the physical assistance of another person or a device to move, as determined by the assessment.
The hours of the day that residents are normally awake, as set out in the shift chart ([WAKING HOURS]).
A staff person who assists residents with activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living or medication, and who meets the qualifications in TRN-01.
The written schedule that shows each shift, the number and type of staff, and the duties assigned for each service in the description of services.

procedures: Before each month, the administrator lists every service in the description of services (see POL-15), including ADL and IADL help, medication help, meals, laundry, housekeeping, activities, transportation, 24-hour supervision and cognitive support.
The administrator uses the current census and each resident's assessment and support plan to classify each resident as mobile or as having mobility needs.

The administrator calculates the daily minimum direct care hours on the Staffing Calculation Worksheet: 1 hour per mobile resident plus 2 hours per resident with mobility needs. The administrator confirms that at least 75% of those hours fall in waking hours.
The administrator adds hours for assessed needs beyond the minimum (for example, residents needing two-person assist or frequent toileting). The reasons are recorded on the worksheet.

The administrator adds separate hours for food service, laundry, housekeeping, maintenance and transportation. These hours are not counted toward the direct care minimum unless the person is performing assisted living services at the time.
If an SCU is operated, the administrator calculates 2 hours of staffing per day for every SCU resident and schedules SCU staff separately (see SCU-02).

The administrator writes the weekly schedule for [DAY SHIFT HOURS], [EVENING SHIFT HOURS] and [NIGHT SHIFT HOURS] showing the name, role and age-qualified status of each person. At least one direct care staff person age 21 or older is assigned to every shift.

The administrator assigns duties by shift on the shift and duty chart (Attachment A), for example: morning ADL care and medication pass, meals, activities, laundry, housekeeping, evening care and bedtime routine, and overnight checks and awake supervision.
Each shift supervisor posts the schedule and reviews the shift duty chart with staff at the start of the shift. Staff sign the shift log at the end of the shift.
The administrator also confirms on the schedule that a licensed nurse is available or on call and that first aid/CPR and awake staff requirements are met (see STF-02).

The administrator reviews the actual hours worked against the planned hours each week. Any shortfall is corrected within the same week by adding a shift, using a qualified substitute or reassigning duties.

The administrator revises the staffing pattern within 24 hours after any admission, discharge, or change of condition that alters resident needs, and after any new service is added to the description of services.

The administrator reviews the pattern at each quality management meeting (see POL-03) using call-bell or request response, incident and resident-complaint information. The administrator adds staff if the data show needs are not met.
The administrator updates Attachment A and the organizational chart (see ORG-01) whenever the pattern changes and submits updated copies to the licensing office when required.
The owner/operator reviews this policy and Attachment A annually.

responsibilities.duty: Calculate staffing, write schedules and duty charts, adjust staffing to resident needs and review actual versus planned hours weekly.
Ensure each shift meets the schedule, review duties with staff and report shortfalls immediately.
Perform assigned duties, sign the shift log and report resident needs that exceed the plan.
Approve budgets that fund the staffing pattern and review it annually.

documentation: Staffing Calculation Worksheet (monthly)
Attachment A: Shift and Duty Chart for each service offered
Weekly schedules and actual hours worked
Shift logs signed by staff
Administrator Hours Log (see ADM-01)
Staff list and organizational chart (see ORG-01)
Quality management meeting minutes addressing staffing

policies.title: Awake Staff, Substitutes, Nursing, Dietitian and First Aid/CPR Coverage
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800); administrator, shift supervisors, direct care staff and contracted professionals
policies.purpose: To make sure that direct care staff are awake at all times, qualified substitutes cover absences, a licensed nurse and a dietitian are available, and trained first aid and CPR staff are present at all times.
policies.policy: Direct care staff on duty will be awake at all times (§2800.58). When scheduled staff are absent, [AGENCY NAME] will arrange substitutes who meet the direct care qualifications and training requirements, and it will keep a current list of the names, addresses and phone numbers of all staff, substitutes and volunteers (§§2800.61–2800.62). A licensed nurse will be available in the building or on call at all times, as an employee or contractor, and a dietitian will be on staff or under contract to address special dietary needs in a support plan (§2800.60). For every 35 residents, at least one staff person trained in first aid and certified in obstructed airway and CPR will be present at all times. The training will be from a certified trainer. Staff will provide CPR unless the resident has a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order (§2800.63).

definitions.definition: A direct care staff person who is alert and on duty and not sleeping at any time during the shift, including overnight.
A person who fills in for scheduled staff and who meets the same qualifications, clearances and training as regular direct care staff.
An RN or LPN with a current Pennsylvania license, employed by or contracted with [AGENCY NAME].
A valid do-not-resuscitate order or advance directive on file for the resident (see RR-02).

procedures: The administrator schedules at least one awake direct care staff person (age 21 or older) on every shift, including overnight. Sleeping on duty is not permitted, and no cots or sleeping areas are assigned to on-duty staff.
The shift supervisor performs and logs a check of awake staff at least once during each overnight shift. The supervisor reports any violation to the administrator at once.
The administrator maintains a Substitute List of persons who have met all qualification, clearance and training requirements in CHK-01 and TRN-01 before working a shift.
When a staff person calls off, the shift supervisor contacts the administrator or designee, who calls substitutes in order from the Substitute List until the shift is covered. Each attempt is logged.

Before a substitute starts, the supervisor confirms the substitute's clearance and training are on file, reviews fire and emergency procedures and resident-specific needs, and records this on the Substitute Orientation Checklist. The substitute is never left unsupervised in this orientation until the checklist is completed.

The administrator keeps a current list with names, addresses and phone numbers for all staff, substitutes and volunteers (see ORG-01), updates it within 5 days of any change, and keeps a copy at the staff station.

The administrator contracts with or employs a licensed nurse and documents the name, license number, and contact and on-call number. An on-call schedule shows who is available each day and night and is posted at the staff station.
Staff call the on-call nurse for any change in condition, injury or medication concern, and record the call and the nurse's instructions in the resident record (see HC-01).

The administrator contracts with or employs a dietitian. The administrator refers any resident whose support plan includes a special diet to the dietitian, and the dietitian's recommendations are filed in the record (see DL-01).

The administrator tracks the number of residents each day. For every 35 residents, at least one staff person per shift who holds current first aid training and obstructed airway and CPR certification is scheduled. For example, 1 to 35 residents require one person, and 36 to 70 residents require two.

First aid and CPR training is obtained from a certified trainer. The administrator keeps copies of certificates and a tracking list with expiration dates and schedules renewals at least 60 days before expiration.

The shift schedule identifies which staff person on each shift is the first aid/CPR-certified person. Shifts without a certified person are not permitted, and the administrator fills them before the shift starts.

In an emergency, staff begin CPR on any resident who needs it unless the resident has a DNR on file. Staff check the resident's face sheet and DNR status at admission and when it changes, and the DNR location is known to all staff (see RR-02 and POL-12).
The administrator reviews coverage each month at the staffing review (see STF-01) and documents any gap, the cause and the corrective action.

responsibilities.duty: Schedule awake, qualified, trained staff on every shift, maintain the substitute and staff lists and the nurse and dietitian arrangements.
Verify awake status, cover call-offs, orient substitutes and confirm first aid/CPR coverage each shift.
Be available or on call at all times and respond to staff calls.
Provide guidance on special dietary needs in support plans.
Stay awake and on duty, keep certifications current and provide CPR unless a DNR is on file.

documentation: Overnight awake-staff check log
Substitute List and Substitute Orientation Checklists
Current list of staff, substitutes and volunteers with names, addresses and phone numbers
Nurse and dietitian contracts or employment records and on-call schedule
Call-off and coverage log
First aid, obstructed airway and CPR certificates and expiration tracking list
Shift schedules showing the certified person on each shift

policies.category: 4. Educational and training qualifications of staff to be hired (including specialty populations)
policies.title: Staff Qualifications and Required Training, Including Dementia and Specialty Populations
policies.applies_to: ALR (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800; PCH parallel under Ch. 2600); all administrative, direct care, ancillary and substitute staff and volunteers
policies.purpose: To set the educational qualifications and required training for staff to be hired, including training required to serve residents with dementia and other specialty populations.
policies.policy: This policy meets checklist item 4, "the educational and training qualifications of staff to be hired including training required to serve specialty populations, such as Alzheimer's Disease or other related Dementia, Brain Injury, Intellectual Disabilities and Mental Health" (checklist cite § 2600.54(a); § 2600.60, § 2600.63(a)–(b), § 2600.65(a)–(b), § 2600.182(b), § 2600.190(a)–(b); ALR equivalents §§2800.54, 2800.60, 2800.63, 2800.65, 2800.69, 2800.182 and 2800.190). Direct care staff will be at least 18 years old, hold a high school diploma, a GED or active status on the Pennsylvania nurse aide registry, and be free of any condition that would impair their ability to give care. Volunteers who help with activities of daily living meet the same standards. Food service and housekeeping staff may be 16 or 17 years old. Staff will receive the orientation and training listed below before they perform the tasks to which the training applies, and no direct care staff person will give unsupervised care until 18 hours of training and the competency test are complete (§2800.65). [AGENCY NAME] will also meet the dementia-specific training requirement (§2800.69), the medication training requirement (§§2800.181–2800.182, 2800.190–2800.191), the first aid/CPR requirement (§2800.63), and the special care unit training requirement (§§2800.231–2800.239). Bloodborne pathogens training will be given under 29 CFR 1910.1030 to staff with occupational exposure.

definitions.definition: Staff who provide assistance with ADLs, IADLs, medication or supervision to residents.
The written test given after the required direct care staff training; a passing result is required before unsupervised care.
Training on dementia care required for administrative, direct care, ancillary and substitute staff and volunteers under §2800.69.
A group of residents with needs requiring additional training, such as dementia, brain injury, intellectual disability or mental health conditions.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious material while performing job duties (29 CFR 1910.1030).

procedures: Human Resources verifies at hire that each direct care applicant is 18 or older, holds a diploma, GED or active nurse aide registry status, and signs the statement that he or she has no impairing condition. Copies are filed in the personnel file.
Housekeeping and food service applicants who are 16 or 17 are placed only in those roles and are never assigned direct care. Their ages are recorded on the schedule.
Volunteers who help with ADLs must meet the same qualifications and complete the same training as direct care staff before helping with any ADL.
On the first work day, before any resident contact, the supervisor gives fire and emergency orientation and records the date and trainer on the Orientation Record.

Within 40 working hours of hire, the administrator or trainer provides training on resident rights, abuse reporting, incident reporting and safe management techniques (see POL-05, SAF-01, POL-01 and SAF-02), and records hours and the trainer's name.

Direct care staff complete the initial training of at least 18 hours and a passing competency test before giving any unsupervised care. Until then, they work only alongside a fully trained staff person. The competency test result is filed.

Within 30 days of hire, all administrative, direct care, ancillary and substitute staff and all volunteers complete at least 4 hours of dementia-specific training. A staff person who has not completed this training by day 30 is removed from the schedule until it is done.

Each year, direct care staff complete at least 16 hours of training, including fire safety, resident rights, OAPSA and falls prevention topics. All staff complete at least 2 hours of dementia-specific training annually, in addition to the other required training.
At least one trained, certified person per 35 residents on each shift holds first aid and obstructed airway/CPR certification from a certified trainer (see STF-02).

Only licensed staff, or staff who completed a DHS-approved medication administration course and performance test within the past 2 years, may administer medications. Insulin administration also requires DHS-approved diabetes education completed within the past 12 months. Staff who assist with self-administration are trained as the assessment requires (see POL-14).

The administrator reviews each staff person's medication training dates every month. Staff whose course is more than 2 years old, or whose diabetes education is more than 12 months old, do not administer medication or insulin until it is renewed.
Staff assigned to the special care unit complete 8 hours of initial SCU training and 8 hours of SCU training each year (see SCU-02).

The administrator provides bloodborne pathogens training at hire before exposure and annually after (29 CFR 1910.1030), and offers hepatitis B vaccination as required. Training is recorded with the date, trainer and content (see SAF-05).

Before admitting any resident from a specialty population ([BRAIN INJURY], [INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY], [MENTAL HEALTH], as applicable), the administrator determines the specific training staff need, arranges it through DHS-approved or other qualified providers, and documents completion before the resident is admitted. Training for specialty populations is added to the annual training plan (see PLAN-01).
If the residence does not intend to serve a specialty population, this is stated in the description of services and admission criteria (see POL-15 and AR-01).
The administrator keeps a training matrix for every staff person showing required courses, completion dates and due dates. The matrix is reviewed monthly, and gaps are corrected within 14 days.
The owner/operator reviews this policy annually and updates it when the regulations change.

responsibilities.duty: Verify age, education and registry status at hire and maintain personnel and training files.
Ensure all training is completed on time, maintain the training matrix and remove staff from tasks for which training is incomplete.
Deliver and document training. First aid/CPR trainers must be certified.
Support medication, health-related and specialty training as assigned.
Complete required training and do not perform tasks until trained.

Orientation Record (first day and 40-hour topics)
18-hour training certificates and competency test results
Dementia-specific training records (4 hours initial, 2 hours annual)
Annual 16-hour training records
Medication course, performance test and diabetes education records
First aid, obstructed airway and CPR certificates
SCU training records (if applicable)
Bloodborne pathogens training records

policies.category: 5. Qualifications of staff named in the resident contract or offered services (including clinically licensed staff)
policies.title: Staff Qualifications Named in the Contract and Description of Services
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800; PCH parallel under Ch. 2600); administrator, Human Resources and contracted clinical professionals
policies.purpose: To state the educational and training qualifications of each type of staff named in the resident contract or listed in the offered services, including clinically licensed professionals, and to make sure no service is promised that staff qualifications cannot support.
policies.policy: This policy meets checklist item 5, "the educational and training qualifications of staff included in the resident contract or listed in the offered services to include any clinically licensed professional staff" (cited on the checklist as § 2600.18 and § 2600.61; ALR equivalents §§2800.18 and 2800.61). [AGENCY NAME] will comply with applicable Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations (§2800.18). For every staff type named in the resident contract (§2800.25) or in the description of services (§§2800.220–2800.223), [AGENCY NAME] will state the qualifications required, identify any clinically licensed staff (RN, LPN, dietitian or other), and state whether each is an employee or a contractor. Clinical licenses will be verified before work begins and kept current. A licensed nurse will be available or on call at all times and a dietitian on staff or contract (§2800.60). [AGENCY NAME] will keep a current list of the names, addresses and phone numbers of all staff, substitutes and volunteers (§2800.62). A service will not be named in the contract or description of services unless staff with the required qualifications are available to provide it.

definitions.definition: A job category named in the contract or description of services, such as administrator, direct care staff, nurse, dietitian, activities staff, food service staff, housekeeping or driver.
A person holding a current Pennsylvania license in a health profession, such as RN, LPN or licensed dietitian-nutritionist, who provides services in the residence.
The written chart listing each staff type, its education and training requirements, licensing, and employment status.
The written statement of services offered, including admission and discharge criteria (see POL-15).

procedures: The administrator lists every staff type named in the resident-residence contract (see FRM-01) and the description of services (see POL-15), and records each on the Qualification Matrix.

For each staff type, the matrix states the minimum age, education, license or registry status, and required training, consistent with TRN-01 and ADM-01. Examples: direct care staff are 18 or older with a diploma, GED or nurse aide registry status; the administrator meets ADM-01; the nurse holds a current PA RN or LPN license.

For each clinically licensed professional, the matrix identifies the name, license type, license number, expiration date, and whether the person is an employee or contractor. Contractors are listed on the List of Consultants (see CON-01).

Before a licensed professional begins work, Human Resources verifies the license on the Pennsylvania licensing website, prints and files the verification, and confirms the license is active and in good standing.
Human Resources also obtains the clearances required by CHK-01 for employees and verifies that contractors who work in the residence meet the same clearance requirements.

The administrator confirms in writing that the contract has a written service-to-staff match. For each service, the matrix shows which staff type provides it and that enough such staff are scheduled (see STF-01).

If a service cannot be supported by qualified staff, the administrator removes it from the contract and the description of services before any resident is offered the contract, or does not admit residents who need that service.
The administrator reviews the matrix whenever a service is added, changed or removed, and updates the contract, description of services, staff list and organizational chart together.
Human Resources keeps the current list of the names, addresses and phone numbers of all staff, substitutes and volunteers and updates it within 5 days of any change (see ORG-01).

Human Resources tracks license expiration dates and checks license status 60 days before expiration and again at renewal. A staff person whose license is not active is removed from the duties requiring the license immediately.
Each quarter the administrator audits personnel and contractor files against the matrix and corrects any gap within 14 days.

The administrator confirms annually that the contract, description of services, qualification matrix and applicable laws are consistent, and reports the review at the quality management meeting (see POL-03).

responsibilities.duty: Maintain the Qualification Matrix, match services to qualified staff and update the contract and description of services when staffing changes.
Verify and track licenses, clearances and training, and maintain staff, substitute and volunteer lists.
Approve contracts with clinical professionals and ensure services offered can be staffed.
Maintain active licenses and notify the administrator of any change in license status.

documentation: Qualification Matrix
Personnel and contractor files with license verification printouts
Contracts or agreements with clinical professionals (see CON-01)
Current list of staff, substitutes and volunteers
Resident-residence contract and description of services
License expiration tracking list
Quarterly file audit reports

policies.category: 6. Staff training plan for first 12 months of operation
policies.title: Staff Training Plan and Training Records
policies.applies_to: ALR and PCH; administrator, direct care staff, ancillary staff, substitutes and volunteers
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who works at [AGENCY NAME] is trained before and during employment as Pennsylvania requires. The plan is written, scheduled for the first 12 months of operation, and backed by records a DHS licensing inspector can review.
policies.policy: This policy meets application checklist item 6, 'A staff training plan for the first twelve (12) months of operation' (§ 2600.66(a)-(b), § 2600.65(f)-(g)). Under 55 Pa. Code §2800.66, [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written annual training plan. For each direct care staff person it lists the name, position, duties, required courses, and the scheduled dates, times and locations. The first plan covers the first 12 months of operation. It includes the pre-service training and competency test required before unsupervised care and the 16 hours of annual training (§2800.65). It also includes the annual fire safety, resident rights, Older Adults Protective Services Act (OAPSA) and falls prevention topics, and the dementia-specific training in §2800.69 (4 hours within 30 days of hire and 2 hours annually). The administrator's orientation, 100-hour course, competency test and 24 hours of annual training under §2800.64 are tracked in the same plan and records. The hour counts in this policy come from the Chapter 2800 text cited above. If the home is licensed as a personal care home under Chapter 2600, the Administrator will confirm each hour count against Chapter 2600 for that licensure type and revise the plan before it is submitted. No staff person may give unsupervised direct care until the required pre-service training and competency test are complete and documented.

definitions.definition: A person who assists residents with activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living, or other personal care services, or who provides supervision.
The annual written schedule of required courses for each direct care staff person, with dates, times and locations.
The test that must be passed after required training before a staff person may work unsupervised with residents.
The Older Adults Protective Services Act, covered in annual training together with abuse and neglect reporting.
The 12-month period used to count annual hours. [AGENCY NAME] uses the staff person's hire anniversary for staff and the licensure anniversary for the administrator, unless DHS directs otherwise.

procedures: Before the DHS pre-licensure inspection, the Administrator lists every planned position from the staffing pattern (see STF-01) and assigns a required-course list to each one.

The Administrator builds the 12-month Staff Training Plan. It shows each direct care staff person's name, position, duties, required courses, and scheduled date, time and location. Where a person has not yet been hired, the plan lists the position and is updated with the name within 5 business days of hire.
The plan schedules fire and emergency orientation for each new person on the first day of work, before any resident contact is assigned.
The plan schedules resident rights, abuse and neglect reporting, incident reporting and safe management techniques so that each is completed within 40 working hours of hire.

The plan schedules the 18 hours of pre-service training and the competency test. Until both are completed and documented, the person works only under direct supervision of a fully trained staff person, and the supervising person is named on the schedule.

The plan schedules 4 hours of dementia-specific training within 30 days of hire for administrative, direct care, ancillary and substitute staff and volunteers. It also schedules 2 hours of dementia training each year after that. These hours are in addition to other required training.
The plan schedules 16 hours of annual training for each direct care staff person. The annual training includes fire safety, resident rights, OAPSA and falls prevention topics.

The plan records the Administrator's required items. These are DHS orientation, the 100-hour DHS-approved course and the passing competency test, all completed before employment as administrator. They also include at least 24 hours of annual training from DHS-approved sources.
The Administrator sends written verification of the Administrator's annual training to the ALR Licensing Office and keeps a copy in the training file.
The Administrator chooses trainers and courses from DHS-approved sources only. Each trainer's name and credential, or the course approval reference, is entered on the training record.

After every session, the trainer or Administrator collects a signed attendance sheet showing the topic, date, hours, trainer and each attendee's signature. Certificates and competency test results are filed within 5 business days.

Each staff person's individual training record is kept in the personnel file. It shows hire date, orientation date, pre-service hours, competency test date and result, dementia hours, annual hours by topic, and the date the person was cleared for unsupervised care.

The Administrator reviews the plan against the records on the first business day of each month. Any person who is behind schedule is rescheduled within 14 days, and the reason and new date are noted on the plan.
Substitutes and volunteers are added to the plan on their first day. The Administrator confirms their required training before they are assigned any task that requires it.

When duties change, for example a move to a special care unit or to medication administration, the Administrator updates the person's required courses within 5 business days and schedules any added training before the new duty starts (see SCU-02 and POL-14).
Each quarter the Administrator gives the Quality Management review (POL-03) a summary of training completion rates, overdue items and corrective actions.
At the end of the 12 months, the Administrator writes the next annual plan. The signed plans and records stay on file and are available to DHS during inspections.

responsibilities.duty: Develops, updates and signs the training plan. Schedules courses, verifies completion, keeps the Administrator's own records and sends the annual verification to the ALR Licensing Office.
Collects attendance sheets and certificates, updates individual records and flags overdue training to the Administrator.
Attend scheduled training, sign attendance sheets, pass competency tests and complete makeup sessions when assigned.
Directly supervises staff who have not completed pre-service training and competency testing.

documentation: 12-month Staff Training Plan (name, position, duties, courses, dates, times, locations)
Signed attendance sheets and certificates
Competency test results
Individual staff training records in personnel files
Administrator orientation, 100-hour course, competency test and annual training records with the written verification sent to the ALR Licensing Office
Monthly training review notes and corrective action entries

policies.category: 7. Floor plan/layout (with Elevator Certificate and SCU/SDCU environmental or physical-site evidence)
policies.title: Floor Plan, Living Units, Capacity and Fire Safety Approval
policies.applies_to: ALR and PCH; the physical site, living units and licensed capacity
policies.purpose: To make sure the building, living units and licensed capacity match what DHS has approved. The floor plan, fire safety approval and related certificates must be accurate, current and available for the licensure application and every inspection.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a current floor plan of every level of the building showing all internal and external exits. It is submitted with the licensure application as the floor plan and layout item. If the building has an elevator, the current Elevator Certificate is included. If the residence has a special care designation, the environmental or physical-site evidence is included (see SCU-01). Resident living units meet 55 Pa. Code §2800.101. A single unit has at least 225 square feet in new construction after 1/18/2011 and at least 160 square feet in an existing facility. No more than 2 residents live in one unit, and sharing is voluntary and agreed in writing. Each unit has a lockable door with a master key available to staff, a phone jack, a thermostat and an emergency notification system. Egress routes stay unlocked and unobstructed, and each floor has two independent exits (§§2800.121–2800.124). Emergency procedures are posted. Floor diagrams are posted if 9 or more residents live in the residence. A fire-safe area is provided for any resident with a mobility need who is above or below grade. The local fire department is notified in writing. Licensed capacity is never exceeded (§2800.13). Written fire safety approval is obtained before licensure and renewed at least every 3 years (§2800.14). The building is maintained so that residents with disabilities have equal access, consistent with the ADA.

definitions.definition: The maximum number of residents DHS has approved for the residence. It includes every resident who sleeps in the residence, whatever the payer.
The private or shared bedroom or apartment assigned to a resident.
Written approval of the building by the appropriate fire safety authority, required before licensure.
An area protected for residents with mobility needs who live above or below grade.
The route out of the building, including exits and the paths leading to them.
