Signed and dated Initial Assessment
Medical evaluation (FRM-02)
Written certification of ability to meet needs, or written denial and referral
Preliminary and final Support Plans with signatures and resident's copy date
Annual and significant-change reassessments
Quarterly support plan review records
Cognitive screening and quarterly reassessment (special care unit residents)
DHS mobility notification record
Assessment and support plan due-date tracking log

policies.title: Forms Library, Fire Drill Record, Rights Poster and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600); administrator, direct care and medication staff
policies.purpose: To keep a controlled set of the forms [AGENCY NAME] must have: the Resident Rights Poster, the Fire Drill Record and the Medication Administration Record. It also makes sure required postings are current and visible.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a controlled master set of its forms, each with a version date, and reviews every form at least annually. This policy meets 55 Pa. Code §2600.41 (item 10(b) – Resident Rights Poster), 55 Pa. Code §2600.132(c) (item 10(c) – Fire Drill Record) and 55 Pa. Code §2600.187(a) (item 10(h) – Medication Administration Record). The assisted living equivalents are §2800.41, §2800.132(c) and §2800.187(a). The DHS rights poster is posted in a public place. Residents and designated persons are told of their rights at admission in a language or mode they understand, receive a copy, and sign an acknowledgment. A written record is made of every fire drill. A medication administration record is kept for each resident and each administration. In the ALR, the residence also posts the current license, the current inspection summary and a copy of Ch. 2800 in a conspicuous public place (§2800.3).

definitions.definition: The one approved copy of each form, kept by the administrator with its version date. Staff print working copies from it.
The written record of each drill: date, time, type, exit used, evacuation time, participants and problems found.
The record made each time a medication is given, refused or missed, signed by the person who gave it.
A person the resident has chosen to receive notices and help with decisions, as named in the resident's file.

procedures: The administrator keeps a forms index listing every form, its purpose, its version date, the owner and the next review date. The index includes the Resident Rights Poster, Fire Drill Record, Medication Administration Record, assessment and support plan forms (FRM-03), contract forms (FRM-01) and the incident report form.
Only the administrator or designee changes a master form. A changed form gets a new version date. The old version is marked superseded and kept for 12 months.
Staff print working copies from the master set. They do not copy forms from other homes or use handwritten substitutes.

Rights poster: the administrator obtains the current DHS Resident Rights poster and posts it in a conspicuous public place. Staff check monthly that it is present, legible and current. The BHSL complaint line, 1-877-401-8835, is posted in large print next to it (POL-07).

At admission, the administrator or designee explains resident rights and the right to complain without retaliation to the resident and designated person, using a language or mode they understand (RR-03).

The resident or designated person receives a copy of the rights and signs the acknowledgment. The signed copy goes in the resident record. If the resident cannot sign, staff record the reason and the witness.
Fire drills: the administrator schedules an unannounced drill every month, varying the day, time and exit used. At least one drill every 6 months is held during sleeping hours (SAF-04).

The staff person leading the drill completes the Fire Drill Record for every drill, with the date, time, who led it, the exit used, how long evacuation took, who took part and any problems found. The leader signs it before the end of the shift.

The administrator compares evacuation times with the time set in writing by the fire safety expert. If a drill exceeds it, the administrator records corrective action and repeats the drill within 30 days.
The annual fire safety expert inspection and drill is recorded separately. The expert's written report and evacuation time are kept with the drill records.
Medication Administration Record: a written prescriber order is in the file before the MAR is started (POL-14). The MAR lists resident name, medication, dose, route, time and prescriber.
The staff person who gives a medication records it on the MAR at the time it is given, with initials and signature. A refusal is also recorded. The prescriber is told of a refusal within 24 hours.
A medication error is reported immediately to the resident, designated person and prescriber. Staff document the error and follow-up on the MAR and in the incident record (POL-01).

Posted documents: the administrator posts the current license, the most recent inspection summary and a copy of Ch. 2800 in a conspicuous public place (GOV-01). Staff replace the license and summary within 2 business days of receiving new ones.
At least monthly, the administrator or designee walks the residence with a posting checklist and records whether each required posting is present and current.

Completed Fire Drill Records and MARs are kept in the records system (POL-17). The administrator reviews the forms index annually, signs the review date, and records it in the quality management minutes (POL-03).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the forms library, version control, postings, drill schedule, and annual review.
Runs the drill and completes and signs the Fire Drill Record the same shift.
Complete the MAR at each administration and report refusals and errors as required.
Use only current forms, report missing or outdated postings, and take part in drills.
Explains rights at admission and collects signed acknowledgments when assigned.

documentation: Forms index with version dates
Master set and superseded versions
Posting checklist (rights poster, complaint number, license, inspection summary, Ch. 2800 copy)
Signed rights acknowledgments
Fire Drill Records and fire safety expert reports
Corrective action records for slow drills
Medication Administration Records
Prescriber notification records for refusals and errors
Annual forms review sign-off

policies.title: Fire-Retardant Mattress Compliance
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600); all resident bedrooms and any other room with a bed
policies.purpose: To document that every mattress used by residents of [AGENCY NAME] is fire retardant. This supports the residence's fire safety program and the DHS prelicensure package.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] uses only fire-retardant mattresses in resident living units. DHS asks for mattress fire-retardant compliance as a prelicensure item, so the residence keeps the manufacturer's label or certificate for each mattress. Before buying mattresses, the administrator confirms the accepted standard with BHSL. This policy supports the residence's fire safety program under §§2800.130–2800.131, which require working smoke detectors and fire extinguishers in every living unit and building.

definitions.definition: A mattress that meets the flammability standard BHSL accepts for licensed homes, shown by a permanent manufacturer's label or a certificate.
A written statement from the manufacturer or seller stating the mattress model and the flammability standard it meets.
The list of every mattress in the home with its location, model, serial number or purchase date, label status and certificate on file.

procedures: Before buying any mattress, the administrator calls the BHSL Operator Support Hotline at (866) 503-3926 (9 a.m.–4 p.m. on Commonwealth business days) or the assigned licensing representative to confirm the accepted flammability standard. The administrator records the date, the name of the person spoken to and the answer.
The administrator writes the standard into the purchasing specification and gives it to the vendor in writing.
At purchase, the administrator asks the vendor for a written certificate or the manufacturer's specification sheet stating the standard met by each model.
When mattresses are delivered, the administrator or designee checks that every mattress carries a permanent manufacturer's label. Mattresses without a label are refused or returned.
The administrator enters each mattress in the mattress log: room, model, serial number or purchase date, label present (yes or no) and certificate on file (yes or no).
Labels are left on the mattress and not removed or covered. A photograph of the label is saved with the log.
Mattress certificates, purchase receipts and the BHSL confirmation record are placed in the prelicensure binder and in the property file.
Mattress covers and protectors added for infection control or incontinence must not defeat the mattress's fire-retardant rating. The administrator checks the vendor's statement before buying one.
Housekeeping staff check labels and mattress condition during monthly room checks (DL-02). They report torn, burned or stained-through mattresses to the administrator.
A damaged mattress is removed from use and replaced with a documented compliant mattress. Staff update the log with the removal and replacement dates.
Residents or families may bring a mattress only if it has a label or certificate confirming compliance. Otherwise the residence supplies one.
The administrator reviews the mattress log at least annually and before each DHS inspection (GOV-01). Any gap is corrected within 30 days.
If BHSL changes the accepted standard, the administrator updates this policy and the purchasing specification within 30 days.

responsibilities.duty: Confirms the standard with BHSL, buys compliant mattresses, and keeps the log and certificates.
Check labels and condition during room checks and report problems.
Checks labels at delivery and updates the log when assigned.
Report damaged mattresses and do not place unlabeled mattresses in use.

documentation: BHSL confirmation of accepted standard (date, name, answer)
Manufacturer labels or certificates for each mattress
Purchase receipts and vendor specification sheets
Mattress log with label photographs
Replacement and removal records
Annual log review sign-off

policies.title: Water Source Documentation
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600); the licensed building and grounds
policies.purpose: To document that the residence has a safe water source and a plan to supply water in an emergency. This includes the 3-day water supply required for emergency preparedness.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] documents whether the residence's water comes from a public system or a private source and keeps the water-supply documentation DHS requires in the prelicensure package. Under §2800.107, the residence keeps a 3-day supply of drinking water for residents and staff. If it does not store that supply on site, it keeps a current bottled-water supply contract that can deliver it. The documentation is reviewed annually with the emergency preparedness procedures (POL-09).

definitions.definition: Water supplied by a municipal or other regulated water utility under a service account.
Water from a well, spring or other source owned and maintained by the property owner.
Enough drinking water on hand for all residents and staff for 3 days if normal service is lost.
A written agreement with a supplier to deliver bottled water to the residence in an emergency, used if a 3-day supply is not stored.

procedures: Before applying for a license, the administrator identifies the water source for the building and records it as public or private.

If public, the administrator obtains the utility's name, the account number, the service address and the emergency contact number. A recent bill or a letter from the utility is placed in the prelicensure binder.

If private, the administrator obtains the well or source record, the date of the most recent water-quality test and the name of the testing laboratory. The administrator asks BHSL, through the Operator Support Hotline at (866) 503-3926, which water test records it requires in the prelicensure package. The test results and the BHSL answer are filed in the binder.
The administrator confirms in writing with BHSL that the water documentation in the package is complete before inspection.
The administrator decides, based on the licensed capacity (PLT-01), how many gallons the 3-day supply must hold for residents and staff, and records the calculation.
If the supply is stored on site, staff store it in sealed containers in a clean, accessible area and check the dates monthly. They replace the water as the container dates require.

If the supply is not stored on site, the administrator signs a bottled-water contract with a named supplier stating the delivery time and quantity. The contract is kept in the emergency binder with the supplier's 24-hour phone number.
The emergency plan (POL-09) states how staff provide water for drinking, medication, hygiene and food service during a water outage, and how staff tell residents.

Staff report any water interruption, discoloration, odor or boil-water notice to the administrator immediately. The administrator tells residents and designated persons and follows utility or health department instructions.
A water outage that affects care or safety, or lasts beyond what the emergency plan covers, is handled under the emergency plan and the reportable incidents policy (POL-01).

The administrator reviews the water documentation and any bottled-water contract at least annually, at the same time as the emergency procedures are reviewed and submitted to the local emergency management agency.
If the water source or supplier changes, the administrator updates the documentation within 30 days and tells BHSL.

responsibilities.duty: Documents the source, keeps the 3-day supply or contract, confirms requirements with BHSL, and reviews annually.
Maintain plumbing and any private water system, and report failures at once.
Report water problems and carry out the water outage procedure.

documentation: Water source statement (public or private)
Utility account letter or bill, or private source and test records
BHSL confirmation of required water documentation
3-day water supply calculation and storage log, or bottled-water contract
Annual review sign-off
Water interruption log

policies.title: Sewer Source Documentation
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600); the licensed building and grounds
policies.purpose: To document how the residence disposes of wastewater and to keep the written approvals DHS may require. This protects residents from sanitation hazards.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] documents whether the residence uses a public or private sewer system. A home serving 9 or more residents on a private sewer system must have written sewage-system approval (§2800.85). The residence keeps that approval on file. It maintains sanitary conditions, with no insect or rodent infestation and trash removed at least weekly in covered receptacles, as §2800.85 requires.

definitions.definition: A municipal or authority-operated sewer system connected to the building.
An on-lot system such as a septic tank and drain field or other private treatment system maintained by the owner.
The written approval from the agency that regulates sewage systems, stating that the system is suitable for the number of residents served.

procedures: Before applying for a license, the administrator confirms whether the building is on public or private sewer and records the answer on the sewer source statement.
If public, the administrator obtains a bill or letter from the sewer authority showing the service address and account, and files it in the prelicensure binder.

If private, the administrator obtains the existing system permit, design, inspection reports and pumping records. The administrator contacts the agency that regulates the system and the Operator Support Hotline at (866) 503-3926 to confirm which approvals DHS needs.

If the home will serve 9 or more residents on a private sewer, the administrator obtains written sewage-system approval for that number of residents before applying and attaches it to the application. The administrator does not admit the ninth resident without it.
If the approval states a capacity lower than the planned licensed capacity, the administrator reduces the planned capacity or obtains a new approval before applying (PLT-01).
For a private system, the administrator schedules inspection and pumping at the intervals the approving agency or system designer requires, and records each date and the contractor.
Staff report slow drains, backups, odors, wet areas in the yard or alarms to the administrator on the same shift. The administrator calls a licensed contractor the same day.

If a sewage backup affects living areas, staff move residents away from the area, restrict access and clean and disinfect the area as the infection control policy requires (SAF-05). The administrator records the event and any resident move.
Waste removal: staff keep trash in covered receptacles and remove it at least weekly. Housekeeping staff check the storage area weekly for pest signs and record the check (DL-02).
A pest control contractor is used for any insect or rodent sign. The administrator keeps the service report in the property file.

The administrator reviews the sewer documentation annually and before each DHS inspection. The administrator updates it within 30 days of any change to the system or capacity and tells BHSL if the change affects the license.

responsibilities.duty: Documents the sewer type, obtains approvals, keeps records, and does not exceed approved capacity.
Inspect and pump the private system and repair failures promptly.
Remove trash weekly or more often, keep receptacles covered and report pest signs.
Report plumbing or sewage problems at once.

documentation: Sewer source statement (public or private)
Sewer authority bill or letter, or private system permit and inspection records
Written sewage-system approval (9 or more residents on private sewer)
Pumping and inspection records
Sewage backup incident record
Pest control service reports
Weekly trash and sanitation check log

policies.category: 14. Legal entity statement of members and affiliated facilities
policies.title: Legal Entity Statement of Members and Affiliated Facilities
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600); the licensee, its owners and members, and affiliated facilities
policies.purpose: To state who legally owns and operates [AGENCY NAME], identify any affiliated facilities, and keep that information accurate for DHS licensing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written Legal Entity Statement that lists every member or owner of the licensee and every affiliated facility. The licensee name on the application, license, contracts, bank accounts and postings matches the legal entity name exactly. The statement is kept current, and DHS is told of ownership changes. [AGENCY NAME] follows the procedural requirements for licensure in §2800.11 and complies with all applicable Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations (§2800.18). Only a licensee may use the term "assisted living" (§2800.11). A home licensed only as a personal care home does not use that term in its name, signs, advertising or contracts.

definitions.definition: The legal entity named on the DHS license that is responsible for operating the residence.
A person or entity with an ownership interest in the licensee, such as a shareholder, LLC member, partner or sole proprietor.
Any other licensed or unlicensed care facility, in Pennsylvania or elsewhere, that a member, owner or the licensee also owns, operates or manages.
The exact name registered with the Pennsylvania Department of State or, for a sole proprietor, the individual's legal name.

procedures: Before the application, the administrator confirms the legal entity name against the entity's formation documents and records the name, entity type, address and tax identification information in the statement.
The administrator lists every member, owner, partner, officer and director of the licensee, with name, title and ownership percentage, and has the owner sign and date the statement.
The administrator lists every affiliated facility with its name, address, type, license number and the person's role in it. If there are none, the statement says so.

The administrator checks that the licensee name is spelled the same way on the DHS application, the license, the resident contract (FRM-01), the posted documents, the insurance policies and the staff and organizational chart (ORG-01).
The statement is submitted with the licensure application as the DHS requires. The administrator calls the Operator Support Hotline at (866) 503-3926 if the application instructions are unclear.

The administrator confirms that the application fee is paid. It is $300 plus $75 per bed for the assisted living residence, with the per-bed amount CPI-adjusted, so the administrator confirms the current amount with DHS. A special care designation costs $150 (SCU-03). A personal care home pays the fee set by §2600.11 by bed count.

The administrator confirms before the opening date that the residence has a license, or is licensed for the intended use, so that it does not use the term "assisted living" in advertising, signage or contracts without an assisted living license.
The administrator reviews websites, brochures, signs and the contract (FRM-01) for the correct licensed name and use of the term "assisted living".

The administrator checks for local zoning, building, health and fire requirements and keeps the approvals or permits on file (GOV-01, PLT-01). Violations of health and safety laws are tracked and reported as required by the reportable incidents policy (POL-01).
The administrator updates the statement within 30 days of any change in members, owners, officers or affiliated facilities, and tells DHS about changes that affect the license.

A change of the licensee's legal entity, a sale or a transfer of ownership is not carried out until the administrator has contacted BHSL about the licensing steps required for the new owner. Residents and designated persons are told in writing before the change.
The administrator reviews the statement at least annually, at license renewal and before each DHS inspection. The review date is signed on the statement.
The signed statement and all prior versions are kept in the governance file and are available to DHS on request (POL-17).

responsibilities.duty: Provides accurate ownership and affiliation information and signs the statement.
Prepares and updates the statement, makes sure names match across documents, and reports changes to DHS.
Advises on entity formation and ownership changes (CON-01).
Reviews and approves the statement annually.

documentation: Signed and dated Legal Entity Statement
Formation or registration documents for the legal entity
List of members, owners, officers and affiliated facilities
Licensing application and fee payment record
Name-consistency check of documents
DHS ownership change notices
Annual review sign-off

policies.title: List of Consultants
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800). A Personal Care Home operator under Ch. 2600 adopts this policy with the Ch. 2600 equivalents.
policies.purpose: To identify the outside professionals [AGENCY NAME] contracts with to meet licensing requirements for nursing, dietary and fire safety oversight, and to keep their scope of work, credentials and contact information current and available to DHS.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written List of Consultants naming each contracted licensed nurse, dietitian and fire safety expert. For each consultant the list shows contract scope, license information and contact information. Staffing must meet the assessed needs of residents, and the minimum staffing levels are not a ceiling (55 Pa. Code §2800.60). A licensed nurse must be available or on call at all times. A dietitian must be on staff or under contract (§2800.60). The fire safety expert performs the annual fire safety inspection and drill and sets in writing the time within which residents must evacuate (§2800.132). A consultant RN or LPN working under an RN may complete initial assessments and preliminary support plans when named in the contract (§§2800.224–2800.227). No official checklist items were assigned to this policy. It is part of the manual section titled "List of consultants."

definitions.definition: A professional who is not an employee of [AGENCY NAME] and who provides services under a written contract or agreement.
The person named in the List of Consultants who performs the annual fire safety inspection and drill and sets in writing the maximum evacuation time for residents.
Reachable by telephone and able to respond or give direction within the time stated in the consultant contract.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], identifies the consultant needs for the residence before opening, using the planned staffing patterns (STF-01), the services offered (POL-15) and the resident population (AR-01).
The Administrator contracts with at least one licensed nurse who will be available or on call at all times, with backup coverage named in the contract (HC-01, STF-02).
The Administrator contracts with a dietitian, or employs one, to review menus and advise on therapeutic diets (DL-01).
The Administrator contracts with a fire safety expert to perform the annual fire safety inspection and annual drill, and to set the written evacuation time for residents (SAF-04).
Before signing, the Administrator verifies each consultant's current license or credential with the issuing authority. A copy of the verification is placed in the consultant file.

Each written contract states the scope of work, the services and deliverables, the frequency of visits or on-call availability, response times, fees, the term, the confidentiality obligations (POL-02) and who the consultant reports to.

The Administrator enters each consultant on the List of Consultants. The entry shows name, profession, license type and number [LICENSE NUMBER], license expiration date, firm name, address, 24-hour telephone number, contract scope and contract dates.
The Administrator keeps a copy of the List of Consultants in the licensing file and gives a copy to DHS with the application. It is shown to the surveyor on request.

The consulting nurse's role is written into the contract. It covers availability or on-call coverage, assessment duties and support plan input (FRM-03), change-of-condition advice (HC-01), and any staff training assigned (PLAN-01).

The fire safety expert provides a written report after each annual inspection and drill. The report records the date, findings, the evacuation time set for residents and any corrective actions. The Administrator files the report with the fire drill records (FRM-04) and completes corrections within the time stated in the report.
The consulting dietitian provides written menu approvals and any therapeutic diet guidance. The Administrator files these with the food service records (DL-01).
Each month the Administrator confirms that every consultant's on-call schedule and telephone number is current and has been shared with the staff on duty.

The Administrator reviews the List of Consultants at least annually and whenever a consultant changes. The review checks licenses, contract terms and scope against the current residents' assessed needs. The Administrator updates the list and files the date of the review.

If a consultant is unavailable, ends a contract, or loses a license, the Administrator arranges a replacement the same day. The Administrator documents the gap in coverage and the interim arrangement, and updates the list within 5 business days.
The Administrator reports consultant-related coverage gaps to the Quality Management committee (POL-03).

responsibilities.duty: Selects, contracts with and verifies consultants. Keeps the List of Consultants current and reviews it at least annually.
Is available or on call at all times as the contract requires. Performs the assessment, support plan and nursing duties named in the contract.
Reviews menus and advises on therapeutic diets as stated in the contract.
Performs the annual inspection and drill and sets the evacuation time in writing.
Know how to reach the on-call nurse and use the contact list when a resident's condition changes.

documentation: List of Consultants, with name, license information, contact information and scope
Signed consultant contracts or agreements
License verification copies
Fire safety expert annual inspection and drill reports, including the written evacuation time
Dietitian menu approvals and diet guidance
On-call schedules
Annual review record

policies.title: Staff List and Organizational Chart
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800). A Personal Care Home operator under Ch. 2600 adopts this policy with the Ch. 2600 equivalents.
policies.purpose: To keep a current staff list and organizational chart that show who staffs and manages the residence, who the administrator's designee is, and how on-call coverage works at all times.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a current list of the names, addresses and telephone numbers of all staff persons, substitutes and volunteers (55 Pa. Code §2800.62). The organizational chart shows the Administrator, the written designee, the staff person named for the Administrator's absences, and the on-call arrangements. The Administrator is present an average of at least 36 hours each week in each calendar month, with at least 30 of those hours during business hours. The Administrator also names in writing a designee who has 3,000 operational hours and has passed the competency test, and a staff person for absences. The Administrator or designee is on call at all times (§2800.56). A direct care staff person age 21 or older is in the residence whenever one or more residents are present. When scheduled staff are absent, substitutes must meet direct care qualifications and training (§2800.61). No official checklist items were assigned to this policy. It is part of the manual section titled "Staff list or organizational chart."

definitions.definition: An employee of [AGENCY NAME], including administrator, designee, direct care, dietary, housekeeping, maintenance and other personnel.
The person named in writing by the Administrator to act in the Administrator's absence. The designee has 3,000 operational hours and has passed the competency test.
A person who fills in for a scheduled staff person and who meets the direct care qualifications and training.
A person who provides unpaid services at the residence and is listed on the staff list.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], creates the Staff List before opening. The list has one line each for staff, substitutes and volunteers. Each line gives full name, home address, telephone number, job title, schedule or shift, hire or start date and date of last update.
The Administrator updates the Staff List within 3 business days of any hire, separation, address or telephone change, or new substitute or volunteer. The update is dated and initialed.

The Administrator confirms that each person listed has met the qualification, training and clearance requirements before working alone (TRN-01, CHK-01, PLAN-01). Substitutes are held to the same standard as regular direct care staff.

The Administrator prepares an organizational chart showing reporting lines from the governing body or owner [OWNER NAME] to the Administrator, then to the designee, department leads and direct care staff. It also shows the contracted consultants (CON-01).
The Administrator writes down the name of the designee and confirms the designee's 3,000 operational hours and competency test result. Proof is kept in the personnel file (ADM-01).
The Administrator names a staff person to be in charge during the Administrator's absences and records that in writing on the chart.

The chart shows the on-call arrangement: the person on call, how to reach them, and the backup. The on-call schedule is written weekly and shared with all shifts. It is posted at [LOCATION IN RESIDENCE].

The Administrator tracks hours present on site by logging time in and out. The log is totaled monthly to confirm an average of at least 36 hours a week, with at least 30 during business hours. The monthly total is signed and filed.
The Administrator keeps a list of approved substitutes. Before a substitute works a shift, the Administrator confirms qualifications, orientation and training and records the check.

The shift schedule always shows a direct care staff person age 21 or older on duty whenever one or more residents are present. The Administrator reviews each week's schedule against the planned staffing pattern (STF-01, STF-02).

When a staff person calls off, the shift supervisor contacts a qualified substitute from the list in order. If none is reached, the shift supervisor calls the Administrator or designee, who arranges coverage. The event is noted in the shift log.
The Administrator reviews the chart and Staff List at least quarterly and whenever the Administrator, designee or on-call plan changes. The review date is recorded.

A current copy of the Staff List and chart is kept in the licensing file and at the [LOCATION] where it can be shown to DHS on request. Because the list contains staff home addresses and telephone numbers, it is kept confidential and not shown to residents or visitors except as the law requires (POL-02).

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the Staff List and chart current. Names the designee and the staff person for absences. Logs weekly hours on site and stays on call or arranges an on-call designee.
Acts in the Administrator's absence and is on call when assigned.
Reports staff changes the same day, arranges substitutes and logs coverage events.
Reviews the chart annually and approves changes in leadership.

documentation: Staff List (staff, substitutes, volunteers: name, address, telephone)
Organizational chart, showing Administrator, designee, absence coverage and on-call
Written designation of designee and staff person for absences
Designee qualification proof (3,000 operational hours and competency test)
Monthly Administrator hours log
Weekly on-call schedule
Approved substitute list

policies.title: Affidavits and Attestations (if applicable)
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600), if DHS requires an affidavit with the application.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] submits any affidavit or attestation that DHS requires with its application. The affidavit must be on the current form, accurate, signed by the right person, and kept in the licensing file.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] submits an affidavit or attestation only if DHS requires one for its application. Before submission, the Administrator confirms the current form and its content with the Bureau of Human Services Licensing (BHSL). No one signs an affidavit that has not been read in full and verified as true. Signed originals or copies are kept in the licensing file. No official checklist items were assigned to this policy. It is part of the manual section titled "Affidavit (if applicable)."

definitions.definition: A written statement of facts signed under oath or affirmation before a notary or other authorized official.
A signed statement by an authorized person that specified facts or conditions are true.
The owner, officer or other person authorized to sign on behalf of [AGENCY NAME].

procedures: Before filing, the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], asks BHSL (717-783-3670) or the BHSL Operator Support Hotline ((866) 503-3926, 9 a.m.–4 p.m. each Commonwealth business day) whether an affidavit or attestation is required for this application.
The Administrator writes down the date of the call, the name of the person spoken to and the answer. The note is filed in the licensing file.
If one is required, the Administrator downloads the current form from the DHS website or obtains it from BHSL. The Administrator does not use an older or locally altered version.

The Administrator reads the whole form and identifies who must sign. If the form covers facts about the legal entity, ownership or affiliated facilities, the Administrator checks it against the Legal Entity Statement (LEG-01).
The Administrator gathers the supporting records needed to verify each statement, such as ownership records, clearances and prior licensing history.
The Administrator completes the form. No blanks are left and none are filled with placeholder text. If a field does not apply, it is marked "N/A."
The signatory reviews the completed form and signs before a notary when the form calls for one.
The Administrator makes a copy and sends the original with the application according to BHSL's instructions. The Administrator records the date and method of submission.
The Administrator files the signed copy in the licensing file and the corporate records.
If a statement on the affidavit later becomes inaccurate, the Administrator tells BHSL promptly in writing and files a corrected form if one is required.
If DHS says no affidavit is required, the Administrator marks this policy "Not applicable" with the date and the DHS response.

responsibilities.duty: Confirms with BHSL whether a form is required, prepares the form, submits it and files signed copies.
Reads, verifies and signs the affidavit, before a notary if required.
Makes sure the statements reflect the actual ownership and affiliations of the entity.

documentation: Note of BHSL confirmation of the affidavit requirement
Current DHS affidavit form (if required)
Signed and notarized affidavit copies
Record of submission date and method
"Not applicable" note if DHS requires no affidavit

policies.title: Management Agreements (if applicable)
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800) and Personal Care Home (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2600), if a management company or manager is used.
policies.purpose: To make sure any management agreement is disclosed to DHS and does not shift away the licensee's legal responsibility for running the residence in compliance with the law.
policies.policy: If [AGENCY NAME] uses a management company or manager, it submits the management agreement with the application. The licensee remains responsible for compliance with Chapter 2800 and with all applicable Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations (55 Pa. Code §2800.18). The manager's affiliated facilities are disclosed in the Legal Entity Statement. Only a licensee may use the term "assisted living" (§2800.11), so the manager does not use that term for the residence or for itself unless it is licensed. No official checklist items were assigned to this policy. It is part of the manual section titled "Management agreements (if applicable)."

definitions.definition: The legal entity holding the license from DHS to operate the residence, [AGENCY NAME].
A written contract under which a person or company other than the licensee carries out some or all of the day-to-day operations.
Another licensed or operating facility in which the manager or its owners hold ownership or control.

procedures: Before the application is filed, the governing body decides whether the residence will use a manager. If not, the Administrator marks this policy "Not applicable" with the date.
If a manager will be used, the Administrator obtains the proposed written agreement. It must name the parties, the services, the term, fees, termination terms and who supervises the manager.

The Administrator checks that the agreement states that the licensee keeps legal responsibility for compliance with Chapter 2800 and all applicable laws, and that the manager must follow the manual's policies.

The Administrator checks that the agreement leaves the Administrator and the written designee in their regulatory roles and does not require the Administrator to work fewer than the required on-site hours (ORG-01, ADM-01).
The Administrator checks that the manager cannot hold resident funds, power of attorney or guardianship, or direct how resident funds are used, contrary to the Fees and Resident Funds policy (RR-01).
The Administrator confirms that all manager staff working at the residence meet the same clearance, qualification and training rules as the residence's own staff (CHK-01, TRN-01).
The Administrator checks that the agreement gives DHS, the Ombudsman and other authorized persons immediate access to the residence and records (GOV-01).
The Administrator checks that the agreement and the manager's marketing do not use the term "assisted living" for anyone other than the licensee.
The Administrator lists the manager's ownership and its other facilities in the Legal Entity Statement (LEG-01).
The Administrator submits a copy of the signed agreement with the application and gives any later amendment to BHSL promptly.
The Administrator keeps the signed agreement in the licensing file and has it available at the residence for inspection.

At least annually, the Administrator and governing body review the manager's performance against the agreement and Chapter 2800. The review is written up and presented to the Quality Management committee (POL-03).

If a violation or complaint arises from the manager's actions, the licensee handles it as its own. The Administrator reports and corrects it under the regulatory compliance policy (GOV-01) and the reportable incidents policy (POL-01).

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether to use a manager, signs the agreement and keeps final responsibility for compliance.
Checks the agreement against these requirements, files it, submits it to DHS and monitors the manager's performance.
Carries out the delegated duties in line with Chapter 2800 and the residence's policies.

documentation: Signed management agreement and amendments
Legal Entity Statement listing the manager's affiliated facilities
Checklist of agreement terms reviewed by the Administrator
Annual manager performance review
"Not applicable" note if no manager is used

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Waivers, Inspections and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800). A Personal Care Home operator under Ch. 2600 adopts this policy with the Ch. 2600 equivalents.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is properly licensed, posts its required documents, cooperates with inspections and access requests, handles waiver requests correctly, and corrects violations on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a current license issued by the PA DHS Office of Long-Term Living, Bureau of Human Services Licensing (BHSL), as provided in 62 P.S. §211. DHS makes at least one unannounced onsite inspection a year. It inspects before initial licensure and reinspects within 3 months (55 Pa. Code §§2800.3, 2800.11). The residence posts the current license, the current inspection summary and a copy of Chapter 2800 in a conspicuous public place (§2800.3). The residence gives immediate access to the residence, residents and records to DHS agents, the area agency on aging, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and the Protection and Advocacy system, and to a resident's designated person if the resident asks. Community and legal services groups are given access during visiting hours (§2800.5). Only licensees may use the term "assisted living" (§2800.11). The residence complies with applicable Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations (§2800.18). Waivers are requested only on the DHS form, follow the public comment and resident notice rules, and are never sought for rules that cannot be waived (§2800.19). Violations are corrected within the time DHS sets. Class I violations must be corrected within 24 hours (§§2800.261–2800.269). No official checklist items were assigned to this policy. It is part of the Governance and Administration section.

definitions.definition: The PA DHS Bureau of Human Services Licensing, which licenses and inspects assisted living residences and personal care homes. Main telephone 717-783-3670.
An onsite DHS inspection made without advance notice to the residence.
A serious violation under §§2800.261–2800.269. The penalty is $20 per resident per day and it must be corrected within 24 hours.
A violation with a penalty of $5 to $15 per resident per day.
DHS approval, on the DHS form, to depart from a specific regulation where no jeopardy to residents results.
A place at [LOCATION IN RESIDENCE] where residents, families and visitors can easily see and read the posted documents without asking.

procedures: Licensure fees: the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], submits the application with the $300 fee plus the per-bed fee. The per-bed fee is $75 as set in the regulation and is adjusted for inflation, so the Administrator confirms the current amount with BHSL before payment. A special care designation, if sought, costs $150 (SCU-01, SCU-03).

Before accepting any resident, the Administrator confirms the license is issued. No one is admitted or served, and the term "assisted living" is not used in advertising, signage or conversation with the public, until the residence holds the license. Operating without a license carries a penalty of $500 plus $20 per resident per day.

On receipt of the license, the Administrator posts the current license, the current inspection summary and a copy of Chapter 2800 in a conspicuous public place and checks the postings monthly. The posted summary is replaced within 3 business days of receiving each new inspection summary.
The Administrator posts the complaint hotline number, 1-877-401-8835, in large print and the Resident Rights notice (POL-05, POL-07).

The residence expects at least one unannounced inspection each year, plus a reinspection within 3 months of initial licensure. Every staff person on duty is trained to receive inspectors, to ask for identification, and to call the Administrator or designee immediately.

During an inspection, the Administrator or designee accompanies the inspector, gives immediate access to the residence, residents and records, and takes notes of findings and questions. Staff do not hide, alter or backdate any record.

Access: staff give immediate access on request to DHS agents, the area agency on aging, the LTC Ombudsman and the P&A system. They give access to a resident's designated person if the resident asks. They permit community and legal services groups to visit during posted visiting hours. Resident privacy rules still apply (POL-02, POL-05).
Within 1 business day after the exit conference, the Administrator records the findings, the date and the inspector's name, and begins a written plan of correction.
Class I violations: the Administrator takes immediate action and corrects the condition within 24 hours. The Administrator documents each action, who completed it and when.

Class II and other violations: the Administrator corrects them by the date DHS sets. Progress is tracked on the plan of correction until DHS confirms it, and the plan is reviewed with the Quality Management committee (POL-03).

Residents are notified of violations as the regulation requires. The Administrator gives notice according to the notification process in the Resident Rights policy (POL-05) and keeps a copy of the notice and the date given.

The Administrator monitors the risk of penalties and admission bans. If DHS bans admissions, no new resident is admitted until DHS lifts the ban in writing. The Administrator tells the admissions staff the same day.

Applicable laws: each year the Administrator reviews Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations that apply to the residence (health, fire, building, zoning, labor and others) and records the review. A violation of a health or safety law is reported as set out in the Reportable Incidents policy (POL-01).
Waivers: the Administrator considers a waiver only when it will not put residents in jeopardy. Rights, contract, reporting, fire safety, assessment and training rules are never waived.

Before any waiver request is sent, the Administrator gives each resident, and each resident's designated person, a copy of the request at least 30 days ahead of submission. The Administrator keeps proof of the date given.

The Administrator submits the waiver request on the DHS form. The request is subject to a 30-day public comment period. The Administrator keeps the approved or denied waiver in the licensing file, posts any approved waiver with the license, and reviews it at each renewal.

The Administrator reviews this policy and the other manuals annually under the forms and document control policy (FRM-04). The corporate compliance review covers current licensure status, postings, open plans of correction, waivers and law changes. The Administrator records the date and any revisions.
The Administrator keeps a licensing file with the license, inspection reports, plans of correction, waivers, correspondence with BHSL and the annual compliance review.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the license, postings and licensing file. Hosts inspections, writes and tracks plans of correction, and submits waiver requests.
Receives inspectors and gives access in the Administrator's absence.
Give immediate access to authorized visitors, direct them to the Administrator or designee, and never obstruct an inspector.
Provides resources to correct violations and reviews inspection results and the annual compliance review.
Reviews inspection findings and the plan of correction progress.

documentation: Current license and fee payment records
Posted inspection summary and Chapter 2800 copy (with posting log)
Inspection reports, exit conference notes and plans of correction
Violation notices given to residents, with dates
Access log of outside agency visits
Waiver requests, resident notice proof, DHS forms and decisions
Annual applicable-law review
Annual compliance and policy review record

policies.title: Fees, Deposits, Refunds, Resident Funds and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800). A Personal Care Home operator under Ch. 2600 adopts this policy with the Ch. 2600 equivalents.
policies.purpose: To make sure fees are stated in advance, resident money and belongings are protected, SSI recipients are not overcharged, and refunds are made correctly and on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] states all charges, refund terms and bed-hold charges in the resident-residence contract. The contract is month-to-month, with 14 days' notice from the resident and 30 days' notice from the residence, and the resident has a 72-hour right to rescind. The residence does not take an assignment of the resident's assets as part of a life-care arrangement (55 Pa. Code §2800.25). Residence charges are mostly private pay, and Community HealthChoices generally does not cover personal care or assisted living residence charges. Residents and families are told this before admission. If the residence admits an SSI-eligible resident, charges may not exceed the monthly income minus the personal needs allowance. The residence provides hygiene items, laundry and ADL/IADL help at no extra charge. Third-party payments are not used for food, clothing or shelter (§2800.27). If the residence handles resident funds, it follows the safeguards in §2800.20. Refunds follow §2800.28. No official checklist items were assigned to this policy. It is part of the Resident Rights section.

definitions.definition: The amount of monthly income an SSI-eligible resident keeps for personal use, which is not available for residence charges.
Money belonging to a resident that the residence holds or manages at the resident's written request.
Mixing a resident's money with the money of the residence, staff or other residents.
A charge stated in the contract for keeping a resident's unit available during a temporary absence.
The Pennsylvania law that governs refunds of prepaid charges after the death of a resident age 60 or older.

procedures: Fee schedule: before admission, the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], gives the prospective resident the written fee schedule, the refund terms and the bed-hold charges. The same terms appear in the contract (FRM-01). The Administrator reviews them aloud and in the resident's preferred language (RR-03).

Payment sources: the Administrator tells the resident and family that charges are mostly private pay and that Community HealthChoices generally does not pay for residence charges. If the resident has long-term care insurance or another third-party payer, the Administrator records the payer in the contract (POL-04).

Contract terms: the Administrator confirms the contract is month-to-month, with 14 days' resident notice and 30 days' residence notice. The Administrator confirms the resident has been told of the 72-hour rescission right, and that no assignment of assets to the residence is requested.

SSI recipients: before admitting an SSI-eligible resident, the Administrator computes the monthly charge so it does not exceed the monthly income minus the personal needs allowance. The calculation is signed and filed.

For SSI residents the residence provides hygiene items, laundry and ADL/IADL help at no extra charge. The Administrator does not accept third-party payments for food, clothing or shelter for these residents.
Resident funds: the residence handles resident funds only on the resident's written request, and the Administrator keeps the request on file. A resident may stop the arrangement at any time.

Staff, including the Administrator and the designee, may not hold power of attorney or guardianship for any resident. The Administrator checks each admission for such a conflict and refers the family to other options if one exists.
Resident funds are kept separate from the residence's money and from staff money, in a place or account labeled for resident funds. Funds are never commingled.
Each deposit and withdrawal is recorded in the resident's transaction record with date, amount, purpose, and the staff person's signature. A written receipt is given for every transaction.
When a resident asks for money, staff disburse it within 24 hours of the request and obtain the resident's signature on a receipt.
If more than $200 is held for a resident for more than 2 months, the Administrator offers the resident an interest-bearing account. The offer and the resident's answer are recorded in writing.
Each quarter, the Administrator prepares an itemized account of each resident's funds and gives it to the resident. The Administrator keeps a signed copy.

Personal property: on admission, staff list the resident's belongings with the resident or representative on a dated inventory, and update it when items are added or removed. The residence does not take responsibility for items the resident chooses not to list. The Administrator investigates any report of missing property and treats a suspected theft under the abuse and exploitation policy (SAF-01).

Refunds at discharge: the Administrator refunds prepaid charges within 30 days of discharge. The personal needs allowance and any managed funds are refunded within 2 business days of the day the resident's unit is cleared. The personal needs allowance is also refunded within 2 business days.
Within 30 days of discharge, the Administrator gives the resident or representative an itemized account of charges, credits and refunds. A copy is kept in the resident's record (POL-17).

Refunds after death: for a resident age 60 or older, the Administrator follows the Elder Care Payment Restitution Act. The Administrator pays refunds to the person or estate entitled to receive them, and records the date, amount and recipient (HC-02).
Bed holds: the Administrator applies a bed-hold charge only as stated in the contract and tells the resident or representative of the charge in advance.
The Administrator audits resident funds records quarterly and reports exceptions to the governing body. Any missing money is handled as a reportable incident (POL-01, SAF-01).

policies.title: Advance Directives and Informed Consent Process
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800); all residents, administrator, designee, nursing and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure residents' health care wishes, including advance directives and DNR orders, are recorded, respected and sent with the resident in an emergency. To set out how the residence uses the informed consent process when a competent resident's choices create a risk to the resident or others.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] respects every competent resident's right to make their own decisions, including decisions that carry risk. When a competent resident's choices create a risk, either the resident or the residence may start the informed consent process under 55 Pa. Code §2800.30. The residence gives the resident oral and written notice that includes the contact information for the long-term care ombudsman. Any resulting agreement is put in writing and updated when the resident's condition changes. The resident may rescind it within 30 days. The informed consent process is never a condition of admission and is never used to pressure a resident. The residence also helps residents secure medical care and documents any refusal of care and its efforts to obtain consent (§§2800.142–2800.143). Advance directives and DNR orders on file go with the resident in an emergency, together with the other emergency data required by §§2800.142–2800.143. This policy does not allow the residence to admit or keep a resident with a condition that is excluded under its admission and retention policies (AR-01, POL-16) unless DHS has granted an exception.

definitions.definition: The structured discussion, notice and written agreement used under §2800.30 when a competent resident's choices create risk.
A resident's written instructions about future health care or a person named to make health care decisions, such as a living will or health care power of attorney.
A physician's or other authorized practitioner's order that resuscitation is not to be attempted.
The person the resident has named in the contract or support plan to be contacted and to assist with decisions.
The Pennsylvania long-term care ombudsman serving the residence's area, contact [LOCAL OMBUDSMAN NAME AND PHONE].

procedures: At admission, the administrator or designee asks each resident whether they have an advance directive, health care power of attorney, living will or DNR order. Asking is voluntary and is not a condition of admission.
If the resident has one, staff copy it, place it in the resident record in the location listed in the Documentation section, and flag the front of the record so staff can find it quickly.

If the resident has none, staff offer general information on request and refer the resident to their physician or legal counsel. Staff never complete the document for the resident or tell them what to choose.

The nurse or designee checks that any DNR order is signed by a physician or other authorized practitioner and is current. The designee notes the date reviewed on the resident's emergency information sheet.

The administrator or designee keeps an emergency information sheet for each resident. It lists diagnoses, allergies, current medications, physician, designated person and the location of the advance directive and DNR. It is updated whenever any of that information changes and at least at each quarterly support plan review.

The informed consent process may be started by either party when a competent resident's choices create a risk, for example refusing a recommended service, declining a diet, or choosing to engage in a risky activity. Any staff person who sees such a situation tells the administrator or designee the same day.

The administrator or designee meets with the resident and, if the resident wishes, the designated person or a person of the resident's choosing. The meeting is held in a private place and in a language or mode the resident understands (see RR-03).

At that meeting the administrator or designee gives the resident oral notice and written notice of the identified risk, the options available, the likely consequences, and the ombudsman's name and phone number.

The resident's decision is respected. Staff do not threaten discharge or other retaliation for a resident's choice and do not make participation in the process a condition of admission or of continued stay.

If the resident and the residence reach an agreement, it is written out. It describes the risk, the resident's choice, what the residence will and will not do, and any steps to reduce the risk. The resident signs, the administrator or designee signs, and the resident receives a copy.

The administrator or designee tells the resident, orally and in writing, that the resident may rescind the agreement within 30 days. If the resident rescinds, the rescission is recorded in writing the same day and the previous arrangement is restored.

When the resident's condition changes, the nurse or designee notifies the administrator and the agreement is reviewed and updated in writing. The updated agreement is signed and a copy given to the resident.
The agreement and the resident's choice are reflected in the support plan at the next update (see FRM-03). Support plan changes are explained to the resident.

When a resident refuses medical care, staff document the refusal, the efforts made to explain the risk and obtain consent, the physician notification, and the designated person notification if the resident agrees, as required by §§2800.142–2800.143.

If a resident may lack capacity to decide, the nurse or designee contacts the physician for an evaluation and the residence follows the resident's advance directive and the instructions of the person legally authorized to decide. The residence does not use the informed consent process for a resident who lacks capacity.

When a resident is sent to a hospital or other provider, staff send a copy of the emergency information sheet, medication list and any advance directive and DNR order with the resident, and tell the receiving provider verbally that these are included (see HC-01 and POL-12).

When the resident returns, staff compare any new orders from the hospital, including DNR status, with the resident's record, and update the emergency information sheet and the copies on file the same day.

The administrator reviews all informed consent agreements and refusals at least quarterly as part of the quality management plan (POL-03) and corrects any use of the process that was not voluntary, not documented or not updated.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure the informed consent process is followed, review all agreements, and ensure it is never made a condition of admission.
Collect and verify advance directives and DNR orders, keep the emergency information sheet current, meet with residents, and prepare written agreements.
Report resident refusals and risky choices to the administrator or designee the same day and know where emergency information is kept.
Make their own decisions, provide copies of their directives, and tell staff of changes.

Emergency information sheet, updated with each change

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800); all staff, applicants, residents and visitors
policies.purpose: To make sure no applicant or resident is discriminated against, that rights notices and other important information are given in a language or mode each resident understands, and that accessibility information is disclosed at application.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate against any applicant or resident. Non-discrimination is a listed resident right under 55 Pa. Code §2800.42. At admission, the residence informs residents and designated persons of their rights and of the right to complain without retaliation, in a language or mode they understand, as required by §2800.41. It posts the DHS rights poster, gives a copy of the rights to each resident, and keeps a signed acknowledgment. The residence follows Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 U.S.C. 2000d) to the extent it applies to the residence, and the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.). Access to services does not depend on a person's ability to speak English, read, see or hear. The residence discloses the number of ADA-compliant units to applicants at application. The residence gives residents 30 days' written notice of new rules, in a mode they understand (§2800.42). Admission decisions are based only on whether the residence can meet the applicant's needs (AR-01), not on a protected characteristic.

definitions.term: Language or mode the resident understands
definitions.definition: The resident's preferred spoken or signed language, or a format such as large print, reading aloud, Braille, audio, pictures or plain language that the resident can use.
A person competent in both languages and in the terms being used who is not asked to take sides. Staff, other residents and children are not used unless the resident chooses them.
A change to a rule, practice, service or space that lets a person with a disability use the residence's services equally.
A resident living unit that meets the accessibility requirements of the ADA and applicable building rules.
Any adverse treatment of a resident because they complained, asserted a right or used the ombudsman.

procedures: The administrator ensures that no inquiry, application, admission, service, room assignment or discharge decision is based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, marital status or any other protected characteristic.

At first contact with an applicant, the staff person asks and records the applicant's and designated person's preferred language and any need for a different format, such as large print, hearing or vision support, or reading aloud.

For any applicant whose preferred language is not English or who cannot read standard print, staff arrange a qualified interpreter or an accessible format before the rights notices, contract and disclosures are given. Telephone interpreter services or contracted interpreters are listed in [INTERPRETER SERVICE AND PHONE].

At application, the administrator or designee gives the applicant the written disclosures required before admission (see AR-01), including the number of ADA-compliant units in the residence and any waivers in effect, in the preferred language or mode.

At admission, the administrator or designee reviews the resident's rights and the right to complain without retaliation with the resident and designated person, in a language or mode they understand, and gives them a copy.

The resident or designated person signs a written acknowledgment of rights. If a resident cannot sign, the staff person notes why and how the rights were explained, and a second staff person signs as witness.

The administrator posts the DHS rights poster in a prominent public place, together with the complaint hotline number 1-877-401-8835 in large print. Where residents cannot read the poster, staff explain it in person.

When the residence adopts a new rule, the administrator gives each resident written notice at least 30 days before it takes effect, in a language or mode the resident understands, and a staff person explains it to any resident who needs help.
Staff do not use another resident or a minor as interpreter unless the resident specifically asks. Any interpreter used is recorded in the record with the date and topic.

The residence provides reasonable accommodations. A resident or applicant may ask any staff person, who passes the request to the administrator the same day. The administrator responds in writing within 5 business days and records the outcome.

If an accommodation cannot be provided, the administrator explains why in writing, offers an alternative, and tells the person they may complain to the residence, the ombudsman or the BHSL complaint line.
The residence does not charge residents for interpreters, accessible formats or reasonable accommodations.
Staff treat residents with equal dignity in room assignments, dining, activities, visitors and personal care. A staff person who sees discrimination or harassment tells the administrator immediately.

The administrator logs and investigates every complaint of discrimination under the complaint procedure (POL-07), protects the complainant from retaliation, and records the outcome. Where the facts suggest abuse, neglect or a rights violation, the administrator follows POL-01 and SAF-01.
At orientation and annually, the administrator trains staff on resident rights, nondiscrimination, language access, using interpreters and the accommodation process (see PLAN-01).
The administrator reviews language-access needs, accommodation requests and discrimination complaints at least quarterly as part of the quality management plan (POL-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensure nondiscrimination and language access, arrange interpreters and accommodations, post required notices, and investigate complaints.
Record language and format needs at first contact and give disclosures and rights in the right mode.
Treat all residents equally, request interpreters when needed, and report discrimination immediately.
Keep accessible routes and ADA-compliant units usable and report barriers.

Interpreter or accessible-format log

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Admission Criteria and Certification
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800); administrator, designee, nurse, admissions staff
policies.purpose: To make sure each person is screened before admission, that required documents and disclosures are completed on time, that no person with an excludable condition is admitted without a DHS exception, and that the residence certifies before admission that it can meet the person's needs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] admits only applicants whose needs it can meet. Before admission, the residence obtains a medical evaluation completed within 60 days before admission and an initial assessment completed within 30 days before admission (55 Pa. Code §2800.22(a)-(c)). The final support plan is completed within 30 days after admission, and the contract is signed no later than 24 hours after admission. Before admission the residence certifies that the applicant's needs can be met. If they cannot, the residence gives the applicant a written denial and refers the applicant to other options. On application the residence gives the written disclosures required by §2800.22(e), including the non-waivable rights list, the contract, the residence rules and the DHS-approved handbook. The residence does not admit a person with an excludable condition under §2800.229 unless DHS has granted an exception. Excludable conditions include ventilator dependency, unhealed Stage III or IV pressure ulcers, continuous intravenous fluids, an infectious disease in a communicable state, nasogastric tubes, physical or chemical restraints, and a need for 24-hour skilled nursing care. The residence keeps records of any exception granted.

definitions.definition: A condition listed in §2800.229 that prevents admission or retention unless DHS grants an exception.
The evaluation on the DHS form completed by a physician, physician assistant or certified registered nurse practitioner (see FRM-02).
The assessment of the applicant's needs completed by a person qualified under the support plan regulations (see FRM-03).
The written statement, signed before admission, that the residence can meet the applicant's needs.
A written approval from DHS to admit or retain a person with an excludable condition.

procedures: When a person or family inquires, the admissions staff person records the contact, the person's age, current location, care needs, payment source and the date of inquiry on the inquiry log.

The administrator or designee conducts a pre-admission screening with the applicant and designated person by phone or in person. The screening covers diagnoses, medications, mobility, continence, cognition, behaviors, nursing needs, diet and any equipment or treatments.

The administrator or designee screens against the excludable conditions list. If the applicant has any of them, the administrator stops the admission process and tells the applicant that the residence cannot admit unless DHS grants an exception.

If the administrator wishes to pursue an exception, the administrator submits a written request to the BHSL regional office, with the supporting medical information. Admission is held until DHS approves in writing. The administrator keeps the request and DHS decision in the exception file.

On application, the admissions staff person gives the applicant and designated person, in writing and in a language or mode they understand (see RR-03): the list of non-waivable resident rights, a copy of the contract, the residence rules, and the DHS-approved handbook.

At the same time, staff give written information on the cost of each service and of the core package, the DHS contact information, how to see inspection reports, the number of ADA-compliant units in the residence, and any waivers in effect.
The applicant or designated person signs a form acknowledging receipt of the disclosures. Staff record the date and time of delivery.

The administrator or designee arranges for the applicant's physician, physician assistant or CRNP to complete the DHS medical evaluation form (FRM-02) no more than 60 days before the admission date, including a TB test result within the time allowed by the regulations.

The administrator or designee, or a registered nurse, or a licensed practical nurse working under a registered nurse, completes the initial assessment (FRM-03) no more than 30 days before the admission date, and prepares a preliminary support plan.

Before the admission date, the administrator reviews the medical evaluation, the initial assessment, the preliminary support plan, the current staffing pattern and the description of services (POL-15). The administrator decides whether the residence can meet the applicant's needs.

If the residence can meet the needs, the administrator signs the written certification and places it in the resident record before the resident moves in. If the certification date is missing, the resident does not move in.

If the residence cannot meet the needs, the administrator gives the applicant a written denial stating the reason in plain language, and refers the applicant and designated person to other appropriate providers or resources, such as the Area Agency on Aging. A copy of the denial and the referral is kept in the inquiry file.

The administrator or designee reviews the contract (FRM-01) with the applicant and designated person, explains charges, refunds and discharge reasons, and ensures the contract is signed no later than 24 hours after admission.
At admission the administrator or designee reviews rights and complaint procedures and obtains the signed acknowledgment (POL-05). The nurse or designee records advance directive information (RR-02).
After admission, the nurse or designee completes the final support plan within 30 days, and it is signed, given to the resident and reviewed quarterly (FRM-03).

If the medical evaluation, assessment or certification is missing or outside the allowed window, the administrator holds the admission until it is corrected. The administrator does not backdate documents.
The administrator reviews each admission record using an admission checklist within 7 days after admission, and reports any gaps to the quality management committee (POL-03).

responsibilities.duty: Screen for excludable conditions, sign the certification, decide on admission or denial, request DHS exceptions, and keep admission and denial records.
Deliver disclosures and the handbook on application, track the 60-day and 30-day windows, and complete the admission checklist.
Complete or review the initial assessment and preliminary support plan and advise on whether needs can be met.
Complete the DHS medical evaluation form.

Signed certification that needs can be met
